title.zh: 卷二百九十三 列傳第五十二 田錫 王禹偁 張詠
title.en: Volume 293 Biographies 52: Tian Xi, Wang Yucheng, Zhang Yong
title.raw: 卷二百九十三 列傳第五十二 田錫 王禹偁 張詠 Volume 293 Biographies 52: Tian Xi, Wang Yucheng, Zhang Yong

sentences.zh: 田錫，字表聖，嘉州洪雅人。

translations.literal: Tian Xi, style name Biaosheng, was a man of Hongya in Jia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xi, whose style was Biaosheng, came from Hongya in Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 幼聰悟，好讀書屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and perceptive, and loved reading books and composing literary works.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick-witted and devoted to reading and literary composition.

sentences.zh: 楊徽之宰峨眉，宋白宰玉津，皆厚遇之，為之延譽，繇是聲稱翕然。

translations.literal: When Yang Huizhi governed Emei and Song Bai governed Yujin, both treated him generously, extended his reputation for him, and thereby his fame suddenly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huizhi, as magistrate of Emei, and Song Bai, as magistrate of Yujin, both treated him warmly and spoke well of him abroad, and his reputation spread swiftly.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，進士高等，釋褐將作監丞、通判宣州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination in the upper grade, was released from commoner's dress as Associate Director of the Directorate of Works, and made Vice Commissioner of Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 978 he passed the jinshi examination with high honors, entered office as an associate director in the Directorate of Works, and was appointed vice commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎、京西北路轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Academician of Writings and Transport Intendant of the Jingxi North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician in the Writings Office and transport intendant for the Jingxi North circuit.

sentences.zh: 改左拾遺、直史館，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Reminder, attached to the Historiography Institute, and granted the scarlet fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as a left reminder with a concurrent post in the Historiography Institute and was granted the scarlet fish tally of rank.

sentences.zh: 錫好言時務，既居諫官，即上疏獻軍國要機者一、朝廷大體者四。

translations.literal: Xi was fond of speaking on current affairs; once he held the office of remonstrance official, he immediately submitted a memorial presenting one essential point for military and state affairs and four major principles for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Xi liked to speak out on affairs of the day; as soon as he took up his remonstrance post, he memorialized the throne with one critical military point and four broad principles for court governance.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：

translations.literal: Its summary said:
translations.idiomatic: The gist of it ran as follows:

sentences.zh: 「頃歲王師平太原，未賞軍功，迄今二載。

translations.literal: "In recent years when the imperial army pacified Taiyuan, military merit was not rewarded, and it has now been two years.
translations.idiomatic: "When the imperial forces pacified Taiyuan not long ago, no rewards were given for military merit, and two years have already passed.

sentences.zh: 幽燕竊據，固當用兵，雖稟宸謀，必資武力。

translations.literal: Youyan is illicitly occupied and troops should certainly be employed; though one may receive the sage emperor's plan, one must rely on military force.
translations.idiomatic: Youyan still lies in rebel hands and force must be used; even with the Son of Heaven's strategy in hand, arms remain indispensable.

sentences.zh: 願陛下因郊禋、耕籍之禮，議平戩之功，則駕馭戎臣，莫茲為重，此要機也。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty, by means of the suburban sacrifice and plowing ceremony, to discuss rewarding pacification merit; then in commanding military officers nothing could be more important—this is the essential point.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty, at the suburban sacrifices and the plowing rites, take up the question of rewards for pacification; nothing would do more to command the loyalty of military officers—this is the critical point.

sentences.zh: 今交州未下，戰士無功，《春秋》所謂『老師費財』者是也。

translations.literal: Now Jiaozhou has not been subdued and the warriors have achieved no merit—this is what the Spring and Autumn Annals calls 'a weary army wasting resources.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhou has still not fallen and the troops have won no credit—exactly what the Spring and Autumn Annals means by 'a long-stationed army that wastes wealth.'

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖人不務廣疆士，惟務廣德業，聲教遠被，自當來賓。

translations.literal: I have heard that the sage does not strive to extend territory but only to extend virtue and achievement; when civilizing influence spreads afar, guests will come of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a sage ruler does not labor to widen his borders but to enlarge his virtue; when his civilizing influence reaches far, distant peoples come as guests of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 周成王時，越裳九譯來貢，且曰：『天無迅風疾雨、海不揚波三年矣。

translations.literal: In the time of King Cheng of Zhou, the Yue people came to pay tribute through nine interpreters, saying: 'For three years there have been no swift winds or violent rains in heaven, nor waves raised on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of King Cheng of Zhou, envoys from Yue came through nine relays of interpreters to offer tribute, saying: 'For three years heaven has sent no sudden gales or driving rains, and the sea has raised no waves.

sentences.zh: 意者中國其有聖人乎？

translations.literal: 'Perhaps China has a sage?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the Middle Kingdom has produced a sage?

sentences.zh: 盍往朝之。

translations.literal: Why not go and pay court to him?
translations.idiomatic: Why not go and pay court to him?

sentences.zh: 』交州瘴海，得之如獲石田，臣願陛下務修德以來遠，無鈍兵以挫銳，又何必以蕞爾蠻夷，上勞震怒乎？

translations.literal: ' Jiaozhou is malarial sea-country; gaining it would be like gaining stony fields. I wish Your Majesty would devote yourself to cultivating virtue to attract the distant, not dull arms to blunt keenness—why must such paltry barbarians stir Your Majesty's wrath?
translations.idiomatic: ' Jiaozhou lies in malarial seas; to take it would be like winning a field of stones. I beg Your Majesty to cultivate virtue to draw the distant near, not to blunt your armies and dull their edge—why trouble Your Majesty's august anger over so petty a barbarian people?

sentences.zh: 此大體之一也。

translations.literal: This is the first of the major principles.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first of the four broad principles.

sentences.zh: 今諫官不聞廷爭，給事中不聞封駁，左右史不聞升陛軒、記言動，豈聖朝美事乎？

translations.literal: Now one does not hear remonstrance officials disputing at court, supervising secretaries not returning sealed memorials, or left and right historiographers not ascending the hall steps to record words and actions—is this a fine thing for a sage dynasty?
translations.idiomatic: Today remonstrance officials are not heard debating at court, supervising secretaries are not heard returning memorials for revision, and court historians are not heard mounting the hall steps to record the ruler's words and deeds—is this worthy of a sage dynasty?

sentences.zh: 又御史不敢彈奏，中書舍人未嘗訪以政事，集賢院雖有書籍而無職官，秘書省雖有職官而無圖籍。

translations.literal: Moreover censors dare not impeach, secretariat drafters are never consulted on government affairs, the Hall of Assembled Worthies has books but no officials, and the Secretariat has officials but no maps and records.
translations.idiomatic: Censors no longer dare to impeach; secretariat drafters are never asked about policy; the Hall of Assembled Worthies holds books but lacks staff; the Secretariat has staff but lacks maps and archives.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下擇才任人，使各司其局，苟職業修舉，則威儀自嚴。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would select talent and assign men, causing each to manage his office; if duties are well performed, then majesty will naturally be strict.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to choose able men and put each in his proper post; if every office does its work, court dignity will enforce itself.

sentences.zh: 此大體之二也。

translations.literal: This is the second of the major principles.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second broad principle.

sentences.zh: 爾者寓縣平寧，京師富庶。

translations.literal: Recently the districts have been peaceful and the capital prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Of late the realm has been tranquil and the capital affluent.

sentences.zh: 軍營馬監，靡不恢崇；

translations.literal: Army camps and horse studs, none not grandly enlarged;
translations.idiomatic: Army barracks and horse studs have all been lavishly expanded;

sentences.zh: 佛寺道宮，悉皆輪奐。

translations.literal: Buddhist temples and Daoist abbeys, all splendidly adorned.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist temples and Daoist monasteries have all been made resplendent.

sentences.zh: 加又辟西苑，廣御池，雖周之靈囿，漢之昆明，未足為比。

translations.literal: Moreover the Western Park was opened and the imperial pool widened; even Zhou's Spirit Park and Han's Kunming Pool would not suffice for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Park has been opened and the imperial lake enlarged—even Zhou's royal park and Han's Kunming Pool pale beside them.

sentences.zh: 而尚書省湫隘尤甚，郎曹無本局，尚書無廳事。

translations.literal: Yet the Department of State Affairs is especially cramped and narrow; bureau sections have no proper offices, and ministers have no hall for business.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Department of State Affairs is more cramped than ever: section chiefs have no proper offices, and ministers have no halls in which to conduct affairs.

sentences.zh: 九寺三監，寓天街之兩廊，貢院就武成王廟，是豈太平之制度邪？

translations.literal: The nine directorates and three commissions lodge in the two corridors of Heaven Street, and the examination compound adjoins the Temple of the Martial Completion King—is this a system fit for an age of great peace?
translations.idiomatic: The nine directorates and three commissions are housed in corridors along the imperial avenue, and the examination grounds sit beside the Temple of the Martial Completion King—is this how institutions should look in an age of peace?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下別修省寺，用列職官。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would separately repair the ministries and directorates and use them to array the officials in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to rebuild the ministries and directorates properly so that each office may stand in its rightful place.

sentences.zh: 此大體之三也。

translations.literal: This is the third of the major principles.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third broad principle.

sentences.zh: 案獄官令，枷杻有短長，鉗鎖有輕重，尺寸斤兩，並載刑書，未聞以鐵為枷者也。

translations.literal: The regulations for prison cases specify that cangues and fetters have long and short, manacles and locks light and heavy; dimensions and weights are all recorded in the penal code—one has not heard of making cangues of iron.
translations.idiomatic: Prison regulations prescribe the length of cangues and the weight of fetters; every measure is set down in the penal code—nowhere does the law authorize iron cangues.

sentences.zh: 昔唐太宗觀《明堂圖》，見人之五藏皆麗於背，遂減徒刑。

translations.literal: Formerly when Emperor Taizong of Tang viewed the Hall of Brightness diagram and saw that the five viscera of man all face the back, he accordingly reduced penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Emperor Taizong of Tang studied the Hall of Brightness diagram and saw that the five viscera lie against the back, he lightened the penalty of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 況隆平之時，將措刑不用，於法所無，去之可矣。

translations.literal: Moreover in a time of abundant peace, when punishments are about to be set aside and unused, what the law does not provide may be removed.
translations.idiomatic: In an age as peaceful as this, when punishments are soon to fall into disuse altogether, what the law never authorized should simply be abolished.

sentences.zh: 此大體之四也。」

translations.literal: This is the fourth of the major principles."
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth broad principle."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，優詔褒答，賜錢五十萬。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an excellent edict praised and answered it, and five hundred thousand cash were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was presented; the emperor replied with a gracious edict of praise and granted fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 僚友謂錫曰：「今日之事鮮矣，宜少晦以遠讒忌。

translations.literal: Colleagues said to Xi: "Today's affair is rare; you should be somewhat restrained to keep far from slander and jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues told him, "What you did today was extraordinary; you ought to tone yourself down a little to keep slander and envy at bay.

sentences.zh: 」錫曰：「事君之誠，惟恐不竭，矧天植其性，豈為一賞奪邪？

translations.literal: " Xi said: "The sincerity of serving one's lord—one only fears not exhausting it; moreover Heaven planted this nature in me—how could a single reward take it away?
translations.idiomatic: " Xi replied, "In serving one's sovereign, sincerity means fearing only that one has not given one's all; Heaven planted this nature in me—how could a single reward make me abandon it?

sentences.zh: 」時趙普為相，令有司受群臣章奏，必先白錫。

translations.literal: " At that time Zhao Pu was chief minister and ordered the relevant offices that when receiving memorials from all officials, they must first inform Xi.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Zhao Pu was chief councilor and ordered that all officials' memorials be shown to Xi before they were received.

sentences.zh: 錫貽書於普，以為失至公之體，普引咎謝之。

translations.literal: Xi sent a letter to Pu, holding that this lost the substance of utmost fairness; Pu accepted blame and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wrote to Zhao Pu that this violated the principle of perfect impartiality; Zhao Pu acknowledged his fault and apologized.

sentences.zh: 六年，為河北轉運副使，驛書言邊事曰：

translations.literal: In the sixth year he became Vice Transport Commissioner of Hebei and sent a dispatch by post on border affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made vice transport commissioner for Hebei and sent a courier report on frontier affairs that read:

sentences.zh: 「臣聞動靜之機，不可妄舉；

translations.literal: "I have heard that the mechanism of movement and stillness must not be rashly set in motion;
translations.idiomatic: "I have learned that the timing of action and restraint must never be set in motion rashly;

sentences.zh: 安危之理，不可輕言。

translations.literal: the principle of security and danger must not be lightly spoken.
translations.idiomatic: and the logic of security and peril must not be spoken of lightly.

sentences.zh: 利害相生，變易不定；

translations.literal: benefit and harm beget each other, change is not fixed;
translations.idiomatic: Benefit and harm arise from each other and shift without fixed pattern;

sentences.zh: 取舍無惑，思慮必精。

translations.literal: in taking and rejecting there must be no confusion, in reflection there must be refinement.
translations.idiomatic: in choosing and rejecting there must be no doubt, and in deliberation there must be precision.

sentences.zh: 夫動靜之機，不可妄舉者，動謂用兵，靜謂持重。

translations.literal: As for the mechanism of movement and stillness that must not be rashly set in motion: movement means employing troops, stillness means holding firm.
translations.idiomatic: As for the timing of movement and stillness that must not be rashly disturbed: movement means taking up arms, stillness means holding steady.

sentences.zh: 應動而靜，則養寇以生姦；

translations.literal: when one should move yet is still, one nourishes bandits and breeds treachery;
translations.idiomatic: If one should act yet holds back, one nourishes enemies and breeds treachery;

sentences.zh: 應靜而動，則失時以敗事。

translations.literal: when one should be still yet moves, one loses the moment and ruins the affair.
translations.idiomatic: if one should hold firm yet stirs, one misses the moment and ruins the enterprise.

sentences.zh: 動靜中節，乃得其宜。

translations.literal: When movement and stillness hit the measure, then one obtains what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Only when movement and stillness strike the right measure does one achieve what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 今北鄙繹騷，蓋亦有以居邊任者，規羊馬細利為捷，矜捕斬小勝為功，賈怨結仇，興戎致寇，職此之由。

translations.literal: Now the northern marches are continuously disturbed—probably because those holding border posts take scheming for small profit in sheep and horses as cleverness, pride themselves on capturing and beheading for small victories as achievement, buy resentment and forge enmity, raise arms and bring on invaders—the duty lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier is in constant turmoil largely because border commanders treat petty profits in sheep and horses as clever policy, boast of minor captures and killings as great victories, buy resentment and forge vendettas, and thereby stir war and invite raids—that is where the trouble begins.

sentences.zh: 前歲邊陲俶擾，親迂革輅，戎騎既退，萬乘方歸。

translations.literal: The year before last the border was suddenly disturbed; the Son of Heaven personally diverted the imperial carriage; once the barbarian horsemen had withdrawn, the ten-thousand-chariot ruler only then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Two years ago the frontier flared up and the emperor himself took the field; only after the enemy horsemen withdrew did the imperial procession return.

sentences.zh: 是皆失我機先，落其術內，勞煩耗斁，可勝言哉？

translations.literal: All these lost our initiative first, fell within their stratagems, and brought labor, trouble, consumption, and exhaustion—can it all be told?
translations.idiomatic: In every case we lost the initiative, fell into their schemes, and paid in toil, trouble, and wasted resources—words can scarcely compass the cost.

sentences.zh: 伏願申飭將帥，慎固封守，勿尚小功。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that generals and commanders be sternly admonished, carefully to secure and guard the borders, and not to esteem small achievements.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that generals and commanders be sharply warned to hold the frontier defenses with care and not to chase petty victories.

sentences.zh: 許通互市，俘獲蕃口，撫而還之。

translations.literal: Permit mutual markets, and when barbarian persons are captured, comfort them and return them.
translations.idiomatic: Allow border trade, and when frontier peoples are taken captive, treat them kindly and send them home.

sentences.zh: 如此不出五載，河朔之民，得務農業，亭障之地，可積軍諸。

translations.literal: If this is done, within five years the people of Heshuo may devote themselves to agriculture, and at the barrier posts military stores may be accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Within five years the people north of the Yellow River could return to farming, and the frontier posts could stockpile supplies for the army.

sentences.zh: 然後待其亂而取之則克，乘其衰而兵之則降，既心服而忘歸，則力省而功倍。

translations.literal: Then afterward, waiting until they are in disorder and taking them, one will overcome; riding their decline and attacking with troops, they will submit; once hearts are subdued and they forget returning home, then effort is saved and achievement doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Then, when they fall into disorder, you may take them and prevail; when they weaken, you may strike and they will submit; once their hearts are won and they cease to think of returning home, effort will be halved and success doubled.

sentences.zh: 誠願考古道，務遠圖，示綏懷萬國之心，用駕馭四夷之策，事戒輒發，理貴深謀，所謂安危之理，不可輕言者。

translations.literal: I sincerely wish to examine the ancient Way, devote effort to far-reaching plans, display a heart that soothes and cherishes the myriad states, employ the strategy of commanding the four barbarians, take warning that affairs must not be rashly launched, and hold precious deep deliberation in principle—this is what is meant by the principle of security and danger that must not be lightly spoken.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly ask Your Majesty to study the ancient Way, pursue far-sighted plans, show a heart that embraces all nations in peace, and apply the art of governing the four frontier peoples—let affairs be undertaken only after grave warning against rash action and let principle be honored through deep counsel; this is what I mean by the logic of security and peril that must not be spoken of lightly.

sentences.zh: 國家務大體，求至治則安；

translations.literal: When the state devotes itself to major principles and seeks utmost governance, then there is security;
translations.idiomatic: When the state attends to great principles and pursues perfect governance, it is secure;

sentences.zh: 舍近謀遠，勞而無功則危。

translations.literal: when one abandons the near to scheme for the far, laboring without achievement, then there is danger.
translations.idiomatic: when it abandons what is near to scheme for what is far, toiling without result, it falls into peril.

sentences.zh: 為君有常道，為臣有常職，是務大體也。

translations.literal: For the ruler there is a constant Way, for the minister a constant duty—this is devoting oneself to major principles.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler has his constant Way and the minister his constant duty—that is what it means to attend to great principles.

sentences.zh: 上不拒諫，下不隱情，是求至治也。

translations.literal: Above, not rejecting remonstrance; below, not concealing circumstances—this is seeking utmost governance.
translations.idiomatic: Above, not rejecting remonstrance; below, not concealing the truth—that is how one pursues perfect governance.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝躬秉武節，登單于之台；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han personally took up military authority and ascended the Chanyu's terrace;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han personally took up arms and climbed the Chanyu's terrace;

sentences.zh: 唐太宗手結雨衣，伐遼東之國：則是舍近謀遠也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang tied rain-coats with his own hands and attacked the state of Liaodong: these are cases of abandoning the near to scheme for the far.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong of Tang tied his own rain cloak and marched against Liaodong—examples of abandoning the near for the distant.

sentences.zh: 沙漠窮荒，得之無用，則是勞而無功也。

translations.literal: Desert wastes and remote barrens—gaining them is of no use; this is laboring without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Desert wastes and barren frontiers are useless even when taken—that is toil without gain.

sentences.zh: 在位之臣，敢言者少，言而見聽，未必蒙福，言而不從，方且虞禍，欲下不隱情得乎？

translations.literal: Among officials in office, few dare to speak; if they speak and are heeded, they may not necessarily receive blessing; if they speak and are not followed, they are just then fearing calamity—how can those below not conceal circumstances?
translations.idiomatic: Few ministers in office dare to speak out; even when heard, they may not be rewarded, and when ignored they fear punishment—how can subordinates fail to hide the truth?

sentences.zh: 惡在其務大體而求至治也。

translations.literal: How can there be devotion to major principles and pursuit of utmost governance?
translations.idiomatic: How then can the state attend to great principles or pursue perfect governance?

sentences.zh: 臣又謂利害相生，變易不定者，《兵書》曰：『不能盡知用兵之害者，則不能盡知用兵之利。

translations.literal: I further say that benefit and harm beget each other and change is not fixed. The Art of War says: 'One who cannot fully know the harm of employing troops cannot fully know the benefit of employing troops.
translations.idiomatic: I further say that benefit and harm arise from each other and shift without fixed pattern. The Art of War states: 'He who does not fully understand the harm of war cannot fully understand its benefit.

sentences.zh: 』蓋事有可進而退，則害成之事至焉；

translations.literal: ' For when an affair should advance yet retreats, then the matter in which harm is completed arrives;
translations.idiomatic: ' When one should advance yet holds back, the harm is already done;

sentences.zh: 可退而進，則利用之事去焉。

translations.literal: when one should retreat yet advances, then the affair of utilizing benefit departs.
translations.idiomatic: when one should retreat yet presses forward, the chance for gain is lost.

sentences.zh: 可速而緩，則利必從之而失；

translations.literal: when one should be swift yet is slow, benefit must follow it and be lost;
translations.idiomatic: When speed is required yet one tarries, benefit slips away;

sentences.zh: 可緩而速，則害必由之而致。

translations.literal: when one should be slow yet is swift, harm must be brought on thereby.
translations.idiomatic: when deliberation is needed yet one rushes, harm follows inevitably.

sentences.zh: 可誅而赦，則姦宄之心，或有時而生害；

translations.literal: when one should be executed yet is pardoned, then the hearts of traitors and villains may at times give rise to harm;
translations.idiomatic: When criminals ought to be executed yet are pardoned, treacherous hearts may someday breed disaster;

sentences.zh: 可赦而誅，則患勇之人，或無心於利國。

translations.literal: when one should be pardoned yet is executed, then men who worry about courage may have no heart for benefiting the state.
translations.idiomatic: when men who should be spared are put to death, the brave may lose all heart to serve the state.

sentences.zh: 可賞而罰，則有以害勤勞之功；

translations.literal: when one should be rewarded yet is punished, then there is means to harm the achievement of diligent labor;
translations.idiomatic: When merit ought to be rewarded yet is punished, diligent service is undermined;

sentences.zh: 可罰而賞，則有以利僭逾之幸。

translations.literal: when one should be punished yet is rewarded, then there is means to profit the fortune of overstepping rank.
translations.idiomatic: when punishment is due yet reward is given, presumption and excess are encouraged.

sentences.zh: 能審利害，則為聰明。

translations.literal: One who can examine benefit and harm is called intelligent.
translations.idiomatic: To weigh benefit and harm carefully is to be truly wise.

sentences.zh: 以天下之耳聽之則聰，以天下之目視之則明。

translations.literal: Using the ears of all under Heaven to listen, then one is perceptive; using the eyes of all under Heaven to see, then one is clear-sighted.
translations.idiomatic: Listen with the ears of the empire and you will be perceptive; look with the eyes of the empire and you will see clearly.

sentences.zh: 故《書》曰：『明四目、達四聰』，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents says: 'Make clear the four eyes and penetrate the four hearings'—this is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Documents says, 'Make the four eyes clear and the four hearings penetrating'—that is the idea.

sentences.zh: 臣又謂取舍不可以有惑者，故曰：『孟賁之狐疑，不如童子之必至。

translations.literal: I further say that in taking and rejecting one must not be confused; therefore it is said: 'Meng Ben's hesitation is not equal to a child's certainty of arrival.
translations.idiomatic: I further say that in choosing and rejecting there must be no hesitation; as the saying runs, 'Meng Ben's wavering is worth less than a child's certainty of reaching the mark.

sentences.zh: 』思慮不可以不精者，故曰『差若毫厘，繆以千里』。

translations.literal: ' Reflection must not lack refinement; therefore it is said, 'An error of a hair's breadth leads astray by a thousand li.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Deliberation must be exact; hence the saying, 'A miss as small as a hair's breadth leads a thousand leagues astray.'

sentences.zh: 自國家圖燕以來，連兵未解，財用不得不耗，人心不得不憂，願陛下精思慮，決取舍，無使曠日持久，窮兵極武焉。」

translations.literal: Since the state plotted against Yan, continuous warfare has not ceased, resources cannot but be consumed, and people's hearts cannot but be anxious. I wish Your Majesty would refine reflection, decide taking and rejecting, and not allow days to stretch on in length, exhausting troops to the utmost in arms."
translations.idiomatic: Since the court set its sights on Yan, war has not ceased, resources have been drained, and the people are anxious. I beg Your Majesty to deliberate with precision, decide firmly, and not let the campaign drag on in endless, exhaustive warfare."

sentences.zh: 書奏，上嘉之。

translations.literal: When the report was submitted, the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The report was presented and the emperor commended it.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙知相州，改右補闕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to administer Xiang Prefecture and changed to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to serve as prefect of Xiangzhou and promoted to right reminder.

sentences.zh: 復上章論事。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial discussing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized the throne on public affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，移睦州。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 睦州人舊阻禮教，錫建孔子廟，表請以經籍給諸生，詔賜《九經》，自是人知向學。

translations.literal: The people of Muzhou had formerly resisted ritual and teaching; Xi built a Confucius temple, submitted a memorial requesting that the classics be given to students, and an edict bestowed the Nine Classics; from then on people knew to turn toward learning.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Muzhou had long resisted ritual and learning; Xi built a temple to Confucius and petitioned that the classics be supplied to students. The court granted the Nine Classics, and from that time the people turned toward study.

sentences.zh: 會文明殿災，又拜章極言時政，上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When the Hall of Civilizing Brilliance caught fire, he again presented a memorial speaking extremely on current government; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hall of Civilizing Brilliance burned, he again memorialized the throne at length on current policy, and the emperor praised and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 轉起居舍人，還判登聞鼓院，上書請封禪。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Diary, returned to oversee the Hall for Petitioning by Drum, and submitted a memorial requesting the Feng and Shan sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant of the imperial diary, resumed duty at the Petition-by-Drum Office, and memorialized requesting the Feng and Shan sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以本官知制誥，尋加兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: With his original office he was made drafter of edicts, and soon after was added Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed drafter of edicts in his existing rank and soon after was given the additional title of vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，京畿大旱，錫上章，有「調變倒置」語，忤宰相，罷為戶部郎中，出知陳州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, the capital region suffered great drought; Xi submitted a memorial containing the phrase 'adjustment and change inverted,' offended the chief minister, was dismissed to Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and went out to administer Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 989 a severe drought struck the capital region; Xi memorialized the throne with wording about 'reversed measures of relief,' offended the chief minister, was demoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue, and sent out as prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐稽留殺人獄，責授海州團練副使，後徙單州。

translations.literal: Because he delayed a murder case, he was demoted and appointed Vice Commissioner of Militia Training at Haizhou, and later was moved to Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For delaying a murder trial he was punished with appointment as vice commissioner of militia training at Haizhou, and later transferred to Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為工部員外郎，復論時政闕失，俄詔直集賢院。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, again discussed the omissions and failures of current government, and soon an edict attached him to the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director in the Ministry of Works, again criticized current policy failures, and soon received orders to serve in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 至道中，復舊官。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao reign he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，遷吏部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, Xi was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne, Xi was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出使秦、隴，還，連上章言，陝西數十州苦於靈、夏之役，生民重困，上為之戚然。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to Qin and Long, on his return he submitted memorials in succession, saying that several tens of prefectures in Shaanxi suffered from the campaigns against Ling and Xia, the living people were heavily distressed, and the emperor was sorrowful on their account.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Qin and Long, he returned and submitted repeated memorials reporting that dozens of prefectures in Shaanxi were worn down by the wars against Lingzhou and Xia, the people were in deep distress, and the emperor was moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 同知審官院兼通進、銀臺、封駁司，賜金紫；

translations.literal: He was made Associate Director of the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments, concurrently of the Offices for Memorials, Silver Terrace, and Sealed Rebuttal, and granted gold and purple;
translations.idiomatic: He was made associate director of the Bureau for Reviewing Appointments, with concurrent posts in the memorial, Silver Terrace, and sealed-rebuttal offices, and was granted the gold-and-purple insignia;

sentences.zh: 與魏廷式聯職，以議論不協求罷，出知泰州。

translations.literal: He served jointly with Wei Tingshi; because their discussions did not accord he requested dismissal and went out to administer Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served alongside Wei Tingshi; when their views clashed he asked to be relieved and was sent out as prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 會彗星見，拜疏請責躬以答天戒，再召見便殿。

translations.literal: When a comet appeared, he presented a memorial requesting that the ruler blame himself to answer heaven's warning, and was again summoned to the informal hall.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared, he memorialized asking the emperor to examine his own conduct in answer to heaven's warning and was again received in the informal audience hall.

sentences.zh: 及行，降中使撫諭，仍加優賜。

translations.literal: When he departed, an imperial messenger was sent down to comfort and instruct him, and additional generous gifts were added.
translations.idiomatic: As he set out, the court dispatched an imperial messenger to comfort him and added further generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 《御覽序》曰：「聖人之道，布在方冊。

translations.literal: The Preface to the Imperial Overview says: "The Way of the sage is spread in written registers.
translations.idiomatic: The preface to the Imperial Overview reads: "The Way of the sages is preserved in the written classics.

sentences.zh: 六經則言高旨遠，非講求討論，不可測其淵深。

translations.literal: The Six Classics have words lofty and aims far-reaching; without lecturing, seeking, and discussing, one cannot fathom their profound depths.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics speak from heights and aim at distances beyond ordinary reach; without study and sustained discussion, their depths cannot be sounded.

sentences.zh: 諸史則跡異事殊，非參會異同，豈易記其繁雜。

translations.literal: The various histories have traces that differ and affairs that differ; without comparing and gathering similarities and differences, how could one easily record their complexity?
translations.idiomatic: Histories trace different paths and record different events; without comparing and reconciling them, who could easily master their tangle of detail?

sentences.zh: 子書則異端之說勝，文集則宗經之辭寡。

translations.literal: Master books have heterodox theories prevailing; collected literary works have few words honoring the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Philosophical works abound in unorthodox doctrines, while literary collections offer little that returns to the classics.

sentences.zh: 非獵精義以為鑒戒，舉綱要以觀會通，為日覽之書，資日新之德，則雖白首，未能窮經，矧王者乎？

translations.literal: Without hunting refined principles as mirrors and warnings, raising essentials to view comprehensive mastery, making books for daily perusal to support daily-renewing virtue, then even with white hair one cannot exhaust the classics—how much less a king?
translations.idiomatic: Without distilling essential principles as warnings and raising key themes to grasp the whole, and without books for daily reading to nourish daily renewal of virtue, even a white-haired scholar cannot exhaust the classics—how much less a ruler?

sentences.zh: 臣每讀書，思以所得上補聖聰，可以銘於座隅者，書於御屏；

translations.literal: Whenever I read books, I think to use what I gain to supplement the sage intelligence above; what can be inscribed at the corner of the seat, I write on the imperial screen;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read, I seek to offer what I learn to sharpen Your Majesty's understanding; passages fit to be inscribed beside the throne I set down on the imperial screen;

sentences.zh: 可以用於常道者，錄為《御覽》。

translations.literal: what can be used for the constant Way, I record as the Imperial Overview.
translations.idiomatic: and passages useful for daily governance I compiled as the Imperial Overview.

sentences.zh: 冀以涓埃之微，上裨天地之德，俾功業與堯、舜比崇，而生靈亦躋仁壽之域矣。」

translations.literal: I hope that with the slightest drop and dust-like minuteness, I may supplement above the virtue of Heaven and Earth, cause achievements to be compared in elevation with Yao and Shun, and also cause the living people to ascend to the realm of benevolence and longevity."
translations.idiomatic: I hoped that this tiny offering might in some small measure aid the virtue of Heaven and Earth, lift Your Majesty's achievements to the level of Yao and Shun, and bring the people into a realm of benevolence and long life."

sentences.zh: 《御屏風序》曰：「古之帝王，盤盂皆銘，几杖有戒，蓋起居必睹，而夙夜不忘也。

translations.literal: The Preface to the Imperial Screen says: "Ancient emperors and kings inscribed all bowls and dishes, and had warnings on tables and staffs—probably because in rising and resting they must see them, and from early to late they do not forget.
translations.idiomatic: The preface to the Imperial Screen reads: "Ancient rulers inscribed their bowls and dishes and placed warnings on tables and staffs, so that in every moment of daily life they would see them and never forget them from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 湯之《盤銘》曰：『苟日新，日日新，又日新。

translations.literal: Tang's Basin Inscription says: 'If one can renew in a day, renew daily, and again renew daily.
translations.idiomatic: The Basin Inscription of King Tang says, 'If you can renew yourself in a day, renew yourself day by day, and again day by day.

sentences.zh: 』武王銘於几杖曰：『安不忘危，存不忘亡，熟惟二者，後必無凶。

translations.literal: ' King Wu inscribed on table and staff: 'In security do not forget danger; in existence do not forget perishing; carefully consider these two, and afterward there will certainly be no misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: ' King Wu inscribed on his table and staff: 'In peace do not forget peril; in survival do not forget ruin; ponder these two constantly, and you will know no calamity thereafter.

sentences.zh: 』唐黃門侍郎趙智為高宗講《孝經》，舉其要切者言之曰：『天子有爭臣七人，雖無道不失其天下。

translations.literal: ' Tang Yellow Gate Vice Director Zhao Zhi lectured Emperor Gaozong on the Classic of Filial Piety and, citing its essential and urgent passages, said: 'If the Son of Heaven has seven remonstrating ministers, even if he is without the Way he will not lose all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ' Zhao Zhi of the Tang, vice director of the Yellow Gate, lectured Emperor Gaozong on the Classic of Filial Piety and quoted its essential passage: 'A Son of Heaven who has seven ministers willing to dispute him will not lose the realm even if he lacks the Way.

sentences.zh: 』憲宗采《史》、《漢》、《三國》已來經濟之要，號《前代君臣事跡》，書於屏間。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Xianzong gathered the essentials of statecraft from the Histories, Han records, and Three Kingdoms onward, titled them Former Ages' Monarch and Minister Deeds, and wrote them between the screens.
translations.idiomatic: ' Emperor Xianzong culled the essentials of statecraft from the histories through Han and the Three Kingdoms, entitled the collection Former Monarchs and Ministers, and had it written on the screens.

sentences.zh: 臣每覽經、史、子、集，因取其語要，輒用進獻，題之御屏，置之座右，日夕觀省，則聖德日新，與湯、武比隆矣。」

translations.literal: Whenever I peruse the classics, histories, masters, and collections, I therefore take their essential words and present them, inscribe them on the imperial screen, and place them at the right of the seat; viewed morning and evening, then sage virtue renews daily and may be compared in elevation with Tang and Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read the classics, histories, philosophical works, and literary collections, I select their essential passages and present them, inscribe them on the imperial screen, and set them beside the throne; viewed day and night, Your Majesty's virtue will renew daily and rise to the stature of Tang and Wu."

sentences.zh: 五年，再掌銀臺，覽天下奏章，有言民饑盜起及詔敕不便者，悉條奏其事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again directed the Silver Terrace, reviewed memorials from all under Heaven, and wherever there were words of the people starving, bandits rising, or edicts and commands inconvenient, he itemized and memorialized all such affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again headed the Silver Terrace, reviewed memorials from across the empire, and whenever reports spoke of famine, rising banditry, or impractical edicts, he laid out each case in memorials to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上對宰相稱錫「得爭臣之體」，即日以本官兼侍御史知雜事，擢右諫議大夫、史館修撰。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chief minister that Xi 'has attained the substance of a remonstrating minister,' and that same day with his original office he was made concurrent Attending Censor managing miscellaneous affairs, and promoted to Right Remonstrance Grand Master and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief minister that Xi 'embodied the true remonstrating minister,' and that same day added to his rank the concurrent post of attending censor in charge of miscellaneous business, promoting him to right remonstrance grand master and historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 連上八疏，皆直言時政得失。

translations.literal: He submitted eight memorials in succession, all speaking directly of the gains and losses of current government.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted eight memorials in succession, each speaking plainly about the strengths and failures of current policy.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，病卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year he died of illness, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year he died of illness at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 遺表勸上以慈儉守位，以清淨化人，居安思危，在治思亂。

translations.literal: His final memorial urged the emperor above to guard the throne with kindness and frugality, transform the people with purity and stillness, think of danger while dwelling in security, and think of disorder while in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In his final memorial he urged the emperor to hold the throne through kindness and frugality, transform the people through purity and restraint, think of danger in times of peace, and think of disorder in times of order.

sentences.zh: 上覽之惻然，謂宰相李沆曰：「田錫，直臣也。

translations.literal: When the emperor read it he was moved with compassion and said to Chief Minister Li Hang: "Tian Xi is a straightforward minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it with deep sorrow and said to Chief Minister Li Hang, "Tian Xi was a forthright minister.

sentences.zh: 朝廷少有闕失，方在思慮，錫之章奏已至矣。

translations.literal: When the court had the slightest omission or failure, while still in deliberation, Xi's memorials had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court had the slightest lapse and was still weighing its response, Xi's memorials had already arrived.

sentences.zh: 若此諫官，亦不可得。

translations.literal: Such a remonstrance official cannot again be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: A remonstrance official like this cannot be found again.

sentences.zh: 」嗟惜久之，特贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: " He sighed in regret for a long time and specially granted him Vice Director of the Ministry of Works posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: " He mourned him at length and specially granted him the posthumous title of vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 錄其二子，並為大理評事，給奉終喪。

translations.literal: His two sons were enrolled in office, both made Reviewers in the Court of Judicial Review, and given salaries through the end of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Both his sons were given office as reviewers in the Court of Judicial Review, with salaries provided through the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 錫耿介寡合，未嘗趨權貴之門，居公庭，危坐終日，無懈容。

translations.literal: Xi was upright and aloof, rarely in accord with others, never went to the gates of the powerful and noble; in the public hall he sat upright all day without a relaxed countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was upright and solitary, never courting the powerful; in court he sat rigidly upright all day without a trace of ease.

sentences.zh: 慕魏徵、李絳之為人，以盡規獻替為己任。

translations.literal: He admired the persons of Wei Zheng and Li Jiang, and took fully remonstrating and offering replacements as his own duty.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Wei Zheng and Li Jiang and made full remonstrance and candid counsel his personal mission.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾立朝以來，章疏五十有二，皆諫臣任職之常言。

translations.literal: He once said: "Since I stood at court, my memorials number fifty-two—all the ordinary words of a remonstrance official performing his duty.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Since I entered court service I have submitted fifty-two memorials, all merely what a remonstrance official is expected to say.

sentences.zh: 苟獲從，幸也，豈可藏副示後，謗時賣直邪？

translations.literal: If I obtain compliance, it is fortune; how could I store copies to show posterity, slandering the age and selling straightforwardness?
translations.idiomatic: If the court heeds me, that is fortune enough—how could I keep copies to show posterity, as if I were slandering my own age to peddle my integrity?

sentences.zh: 」悉命焚之。

translations.literal: " He ordered them all burned.
translations.idiomatic: " He had them all burned.

sentences.zh: 然性凝執，治郡無稱。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was stiff and obstinate, and in governing prefectures he had no reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was rigid and obstinate, and he won no reputation as a prefectural administrator.

sentences.zh: 所著有《咸平集》五十卷。

translations.literal: His writings include the Xianping Collection in fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, the Xianping Collection, comprise fifty juan.

sentences.zh: 王禹偁

translations.literal: Wang Yucheng
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yucheng

sentences.zh: 王禹偁，字元之，濟州鉅野人。

translations.literal: Wang Yucheng, style name Yuanzhi, was a man of Juye in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yucheng, whose style was Yuanzhi, came from Juye in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 世為農家，九歲能文，畢士安見而器之。

translations.literal: His family for generations were farmers; at nine he could write, and Bi Shian saw him and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been farmers for generations; at nine he could compose essays, and Bi Shian recognized his talent and took him seriously.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年擢進士，授成武主簿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he was selected as jinshi and appointed Chief Clerk of Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: In 983 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 徙知長洲縣，就改大理評事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Changzhou County and then changed to Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Changzhou County and soon after made a reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 同年生羅處約時宰吳縣，日相與賦詠，人多傳誦。

translations.literal: His fellow graduate Luo Chuyue at the time governed Wu County; daily they composed and chanted poems together, and many people transmitted and recited them.
translations.idiomatic: His examination-year companion Luo Chuyue was then magistrate of Wu County; they composed poetry together daily, and their verses were widely circulated.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，太宗聞其名，召試，擢右拾遺、直史館，賜緋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, Emperor Taizong heard his name, summoned him for examination, promoted him to Right Reminder and attached him to the Historiography Institute, and granted scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong era Emperor Taizong heard of him, summoned him for a trial, and appointed him right reminder with a post in the Historiography Institute, granting the scarlet rank.

sentences.zh: 故事，賜緋者給塗金銀帶，上特命以文犀帶寵之。

translations.literal: By precedent, those granted scarlet were given gilded silver belts; the emperor specially ordered the patterned rhinoceros belt to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent scarlet rank brought a gilded silver belt, but the emperor specially honored him with a patterned rhinoceros-horn belt.

sentences.zh: 即日獻《端拱箴》以寓規諷。

translations.literal: That same day he presented the Admonition for Duangong to embody remonstrance and satire.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he presented his Admonition for the Duangong Era, embedding counsel in measured rebuke.

sentences.zh: 時北庭未寧，訪群臣以邊事。

translations.literal: At the time the northern court was not yet settled, and the emperor consulted the ministers on border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier was still unsettled, and the emperor asked his ministers about border policy.

sentences.zh: 禹偁獻《禦戎十策》，大略假漢事以明之：「漢十二君，言賢明者，文、景也；

translations.literal: Yucheng presented the Ten Policies for Controlling the Barbarians, broadly using Han affairs to clarify them: "Of the twelve Han rulers, those called wise and enlightened were Wen and Jing;
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng submitted the Ten Policies for Frontier Defense, drawing chiefly on Han history to make his case: "Of the twelve Han emperors, those called wise were Wen and Jing;

sentences.zh: 言昏亂者，哀、平也。

translations.literal: those called benighted and chaotic were Ai and Ping.
translations.idiomatic: those called benighted and chaotic were Ai and Ping.

sentences.zh: 然而文、景之世，軍臣單于最為強盛，肆行侵掠，候騎至雍，火照甘泉。

translations.literal: Yet in the ages of Wen and Jing, the Chanyu Junchen was most powerful, wantonly conducting invasions and plunder; patrol horsemen reached Yong, and fires lit up Sweet Springs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the reigns of Wen and Jing the Chanyu Junchen was at his strongest, raiding at will until patrol riders reached Yong and fires lit the Sweet Springs Palace.

sentences.zh: 哀、平之時，呼韓邪單于每歲來朝，委質稱臣，邊烽罷警。

translations.literal: In the times of Ai and Ping, the Chanyu Huhanye came to court every year, presented credentials and called himself subject, and border beacon fires ceased their warnings.
translations.idiomatic: In the reigns of Ai and Ping the Chanyu Huhanye came to court every year, submitted tribute, declared himself a subject, and frontier alarms fell silent.

sentences.zh: 何邪？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why was this?

sentences.zh: 蓋漢文當軍臣強盛之時，而外任人、內修政，使不能為深患者，由乎德也。

translations.literal: Probably because when Emperor Wen of Han faced Junchen at his strongest, he employed men abroad and cultivated government within, causing him not to become a deep affliction—this was due to virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Because when Emperor Wen faced Junchen at his height, he entrusted men abroad and cultivated government at home, so the nomads could not inflict deep harm—this came from virtue.

sentences.zh: 哀、平當呼韓衰弱之際，雖外無良將，內無賢臣，而致其來朝者，繫於時也。

translations.literal: Ai and Ping, when Huhanye was in weakness—though abroad there were no good generals and within no worthy ministers, yet causing him to come to court was bound to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Ai and Ping ruled when Huhanye was weak; though they had no good generals abroad and no worthy ministers at home, his coming to court depended on the times.

sentences.zh: 今國家之廣大，不下漢朝，陛下之聖明，豈讓文帝。

translations.literal: Now the state's vastness is not below the Han dynasty, and Your Majesty's sagely enlightenment—how could it yield to Emperor Wen?
translations.idiomatic: Our realm is no smaller than the Han empire, and Your Majesty's sagacity is surely no less than Emperor Wen's.

sentences.zh: 契丹之強盛，不及軍臣單于，至如撓邊侵塞，豈有候騎至雍，而火照甘泉之患乎？

translations.literal: The Khitan's strength does not reach Junchen Chanyu; as for harassing the border and invading the passes, how could there be the affliction of patrol riders reaching Yong and fires lighting Sweet Springs?
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan are not as strong as the Chanyu Junchen was; even if they harass the border, could they bring patrol riders to Yong and set fires at Sweet Springs?

sentences.zh: 亦在乎外任人、內修德爾。

translations.literal: This also lies in employing men abroad and cultivating virtue within.
translations.idiomatic: That too depends on trusting the right men abroad and cultivating virtue at home.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為：外則合兵勢而重將權，罷小臣詗邏邊事，行間諜離其黨，遣趙保忠、折禦卿率所部以掎角。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that externally one should combine military strength and weight general authority, stop minor officials from spying on border affairs, employ spies to divide their faction, and send Zhao Baozhong and Zhe Yuqing to lead their commands in pincer support.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that externally we should concentrate military force and empower generals, stop petty officials from meddling in frontier intelligence, use spies to split their factions, and send Zhao Baozhong and Zhe Yuqing to lead their troops in coordinated pressure.

sentences.zh: 下詔感勵邊人，使知取燕薊舊疆，非貪其土地；

translations.literal: Issue an edict to move and encourage border people, causing them to know that recovering the old territories of Yan and Ji is not coveting their land;
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict to stir the border peoples, making clear that recovering the old Yan and Ji territories is not greed for land;

sentences.zh: 內則省官以寬經費，抑文士以激武夫，信用大臣以資其謀，不貴虛名以戒無益，禁遊惰以厚民力。

translations.literal: internally reduce officials to ease expenditures, restrain literary men to rouse military men, trust and employ great ministers to supply their plans, do not value empty names to warn against the useless, and prohibit wandering idleness to thicken the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: internally reduce offices to ease expenditures, restrain literati to rouse warriors, trust great ministers for counsel, spurn empty reputation, and forbid idleness to strengthen the people's resources.

sentences.zh: 」帝深嘉之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply praised it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised it highly.

sentences.zh: 又與夏侯嘉正、羅處約、杜鎬表請同校《三史書》，多所釐正。

translations.literal: He also with Xiahou Jiazheng, Luo Chuyue, and Du Hao memorialized requesting to collate the Three Histories together, correcting many passages.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Xiahou Jiazheng, Luo Chuyue, and Du Hao he petitioned to collate the Three Histories jointly, correcting numerous passages.

sentences.zh: 二年，親試貢士，召禹偁，賦詩立就。

translations.literal: In the second year, when personally examining tribute scholars, he summoned Yucheng, who composed a poem on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, at the imperial examination of tribute scholars, Yucheng was summoned and composed a poem immediately.

sentences.zh: 上悅曰：「此不逾月遍天下矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "This will spread through all under Heaven within a month.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with delight, "Within a month this will be known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 」即拜左司諫、知制誥。

translations.literal: " He was immediately appointed Left Secretariat Remonstrator and Drafter of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately made left secretariat remonstrator and drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 是冬，京城旱，禹偁疏云：「一穀不收謂之饉，五穀不收謂之饑。

translations.literal: That winter the capital region suffered drought; Yucheng's memorial said: "When one grain crop fails it is called jin; when the five grains all fail it is called ji.
translations.idiomatic: That winter drought struck the capital; Yucheng memorialized: "When one crop fails it is called scarcity; when all five grains fail it is famine.

sentences.zh: 饉則大夫以下，皆損其祿；

translations.literal: In jin, grand masters and below all reduce their salaries;
translations.idiomatic: In scarcity, officials from grand master down should reduce their salaries;

sentences.zh: 饑則盡無祿，廩食而已。

translations.literal: in ji all have no salary and receive only granary rations.
translations.idiomatic: in famine they should receive no salary at all, only granary rations.

sentences.zh: 今旱雲未霑，宿麥未茁，既無積蓄，民饑可憂。

translations.literal: Now drought clouds have not moistened, winter wheat has not sprouted, there are no stored reserves, and the people's hunger is to be worried over.
translations.idiomatic: Now the drought clouds have not brought rain, the winter wheat has not sprouted, reserves are gone, and the people's hunger is deeply worrying.

sentences.zh: 望下詔直云：『君臣之間，政教有闕，自乘輿服御，下至百官奉料，非宿衛軍士、邊庭將帥，悉第減之，上答天譴，下厭人心，俟雨足復故。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will issue an edict stating plainly: 'Between ruler and minister, government and teaching have gaps; from the imperial carriage and apparel down to the salaries of all officials—except palace guards and frontier generals—all are to be reduced by degrees, above to answer heaven's reproof, below to satisfy the people's hearts, and when rain is sufficient restore the former state.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty issue a plain edict: 'Between ruler and ministers there are failings in government and teaching; from the imperial carriage and wardrobe down to officials' salaries—except palace guards and frontier commanders—reduce all by degrees, to answer heaven's reproof above and satisfy the people below, restoring former levels when rain returns.

sentences.zh: 』臣朝行中家最貧，奉最薄，亦願首減奉，以贖耗蠹之咎。

translations.literal: ' Among court colleagues my family is poorest and my salary thinnest; I also wish to be first to reduce salary, to atone for the fault of consuming and gnawing away resources.
translations.idiomatic: ' Among my colleagues at court my family is the poorest and my salary the smallest; I too ask to be the first to cut my pay, to atone for having consumed the state's resources.

sentences.zh: 外則停歲市之物；

translations.literal: Externally stop the goods of the annual markets;
translations.idiomatic: Externally suspend the annual tribute markets;

sentences.zh: 內則罷工巧之伎。

translations.literal: internally abolish the crafts of artisans.
translations.idiomatic: internally halt artisan crafts and displays of luxury.

sentences.zh: 近城掘土，侵塚墓者瘞之；

translations.literal: Where earth is dug near the city and tombs are encroached upon, bury them properly;
translations.idiomatic: Where earth is dug near the city and graves are disturbed, see that they are properly reburied;

sentences.zh: 外州配隸之眾，非贓盜者釋之。

translations.literal: among the masses assigned to penal service in outer prefectures, release those who are not corrupt thieves.
translations.idiomatic: release from penal service in the outer prefectures all who are not guilty of theft or corruption.

sentences.zh: 然後以古者猛虎渡河、飛蝗越境之事，戒敕州縣官吏。

translations.literal: Then use the ancient matters of tigers crossing rivers and locusts crossing borders to admonish and instruct prefectural and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Then warn prefectural and county officials with the ancient examples of tigers crossing rivers and locusts crossing borders without restraint.

sentences.zh: 其餘軍民刑政之弊，非臣所知者，望委宰臣裁議頒行，但感人心，必召和氣。」

translations.literal: As for the remaining abuses in military and civil criminal government that your servant does not know, I hope they may be entrusted to the chief ministers to deliberate and promulgate; only move the people's hearts and harmonious qi will certainly be summoned."
translations.idiomatic: As for other abuses in military and civil administration beyond my knowledge, I ask that the chief ministers deliberate and issue orders; if the people's hearts are touched, harmonious qi will surely follow."

sentences.zh: 未幾，判大理寺，廬州妖尼道安誣訟徐鉉，道安當反坐，有詔勿治。

translations.literal: Before long he was put in charge of the Court of Judicial Review; the sorceress nun Dao'an of Luzhou falsely sued Xu Xuan, and Dao'an should have been punished by counter-sentence, but an edict ordered that the case not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was assigned to the Court of Judicial Review; the sorceress nun Dao'an of Luzhou brought a false suit against Xu Xuan, and though Dao'an should have been punished in turn, an edict forbade prosecution.

sentences.zh: 禹偁抗疏雪鉉，請論道安罪，坐貶商州團練副使，歲餘移解州。

translations.literal: Yucheng submitted a defiant memorial to clear Xuan and requested that Dao'an's crime be judged; he was demoted and appointed Vice Commissioner of Militia Training at Shang Prefecture, and after more than a year was moved to Xie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng submitted a forceful memorial to vindicate Xu Xuan and demanded that Dao'an be punished; he was demoted to vice commissioner of militia training at Shangzhou and, after a year, transferred to Xiezhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，召拜左正言，上以其性剛直不容物，命宰相戒之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned and appointed Left Rectifier; because his nature was stern and upright and intolerant of others, the emperor ordered the chief minister to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled as left rectifier; because his nature was blunt and uncompromising, the emperor told the chief minister to warn him.

sentences.zh: 直昭文館，丐外任以便奉養，得知單州，賜錢三十萬。

translations.literal: He was attached to the Zhaowen Hall, begged for an outer post to facilitate supporting his parents, was made administrator of Shan Prefecture, and granted three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Attached to the Zhaowen Hall, he asked for an outside post to support his parents, was made prefect of Shanzhou, and granted three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 至郡十五日，召為禮部員外郎，再知制誥。

translations.literal: Fifteen days after reaching the prefecture he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and again made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen days after reaching his post he was recalled as vice director in the Ministry of Rites and again made drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 屢獻討李繼遷便宜，以為繼遷不必勞力而誅，自可用計而取。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented plans for dealing with Li Jiqian expediently, holding that Jiqian need not be executed by laboring troops but could naturally be taken by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted plans for dealing with Li Jiqian, arguing that Jiqian need not be destroyed by force but could be taken by strategy.

sentences.zh: 謂宜明數繼遷罪惡，曉諭蕃漢，垂立賞賜，高與官資，則繼遷身首，不梟即擒矣。

translations.literal: He said one should clearly enumerate Jiqian's crimes, instruct both barbarian and Han, suspend rewards, grant high office and salary, and then Jiqian's person and head would either be displayed on poles or captured.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that Jiqian's crimes be proclaimed openly, that both Tangut and Han be informed, that rich rewards and high office be promised—then Jiqian's head would either be displayed or he would be captured alive.

sentences.zh: 其後潘羅支射死繼遷，夏人款附，卒如禹偁策。

translations.literal: Afterward Pan Luozhi shot and killed Jiqian, the Xia people submitted in good faith, and in the end it was as Yucheng's plan had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Pan Luozhi shot and killed Jiqian, the Xia submitted, and events unfolded exactly as Yucheng had predicted.

sentences.zh: 「一曰謹邊防，通盟好，使輦運之民有所休息。

translations.literal: "First: carefully guard the border defenses, open alliance and friendship, and cause the people who transport by imperial carriage to have rest.
translations.idiomatic: "First: guard the frontier carefully, restore friendly relations, and give the transport-corvee people a chance to rest.

sentences.zh: 方今北有契丹，西有繼遷。

translations.literal: At present in the north there are the Khitan, in the west Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Today we face the Khitan in the north and Jiqian in the west.

sentences.zh: 契丹雖不侵邊，戍兵豈能減削？

translations.literal: Though the Khitan do not invade the border, how can garrison troops be reduced?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Khitan do not raid the border, how can frontier garrisons be cut?

sentences.zh: 繼遷既未歸命，饋餉固難寢停。

translations.literal: Since Jiqian has not yet submitted to orders, provisions and supplies naturally cannot lie dormant and stop.
translations.idiomatic: As long as Jiqian has not submitted, supply convoys cannot cease.

sentences.zh: 關輔之民，倒懸尤甚。

translations.literal: The people of the capital region are especially hung upside down in distress.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital region suffer most grievously under this burden.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜敕封疆之吏，致書遼臣，俾達其主，請尋舊好。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that border officials should be ordered to send letters to Liao ministers, causing them to reach their lord and request renewal of the old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: I believe border officials should be ordered to write to Liao ministers, have them convey the message to their ruler, and seek restoration of the old friendship.

sentences.zh: 下詔赦繼遷罪，復與夏臺。

translations.literal: Issue an edict pardoning Jiqian's crimes and restore him to the Xia platform.
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict pardoning Jiqian's crimes and restore his Xia title.

sentences.zh: 彼必感恩內附，且使天下知陛下屈己而為民也。

translations.literal: They will certainly be grateful and submit inwardly, and also cause all under Heaven to know that Your Majesty bends himself for the sake of the people.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely submit in gratitude, and all the realm will see that Your Majesty humbles himself for the people's sake.

sentences.zh: 二曰減冗兵，併冗吏，使山澤之饒，稍流於下。

translations.literal: Second: reduce redundant troops, merge redundant officials, and cause the abundance of mountains and marshes to flow somewhat downward.
translations.idiomatic: Second: cut redundant troops, consolidate redundant officials, and let the wealth of mountains and marshes reach the people below.

sentences.zh: 當乾德、開寶之時，土地未廣，財賦未豐，然而擊河東，備北鄙，國用未足，兵威亦強，其義安在？

translations.literal: In the times of Qiande and Kaibao, territory was not yet broad and revenues not yet abundant, yet they struck Hedong and prepared the northern marches; state expenditures were not sufficient yet military might was also strong—where lay the principle?
translations.idiomatic: In the Qiande and Kaibao eras territory was smaller and revenues thinner, yet they struck Hedong and guarded the north; state funds were tight yet military power was strong—why?

sentences.zh: 由所蓄之兵銳而不眾，所用之將專而不疑故也。

translations.literal: It was because the troops stored were keen but not numerous, and the generals employed were focused and not doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Because the troops kept were few but sharp, and the generals employed were given full trust without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 自後盡取東南數國，又平河東，土地財賦，可謂廣且豐矣，而兵威不振，國用轉急，其義安在？

translations.literal: Afterward they took all the several states of the southeast and also pacified Hedong; territory and revenues may be called broad and abundant, yet military might does not flourish and state expenditures grow urgent—where lies the principle?
translations.idiomatic: Later the court conquered the southeastern states and pacified Hedong; territory and revenue are now broad and rich, yet military power has not revived and state funds grow tighter—why?

sentences.zh: 由所蓄之兵冗而不盡銳，所用之將眾而不自專故也。

translations.literal: It is because the troops stored are redundant and not all keen, and the generals employed are many and not self-focused.
translations.idiomatic: Because the troops kept are numerous but not all elite, and the generals employed are many but not given independent authority.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜經制兵賦，如開寶中，則可高枕而治矣。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that troops and levies should be regulated as in Kaibao, and then one may rule with pillow high.
translations.idiomatic: I believe troops and tax levies should be reorganized as in the Kaibao era, and then the throne could rule with ease.

sentences.zh: 且開寶中設官至少。

translations.literal: Moreover in Kaibao the offices established were fewest.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaibao era the fewest offices were established.

sentences.zh: 臣本魯人，占籍濟上，未及第時，一州止有刺史一人、司戶一人，當時未嘗闕事。

translations.literal: Your servant is originally a man of Lu, registered on the Ji uplands; before passing the examination, one prefecture had only one inspector and one revenue registrar, and at the time affairs were never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: I am a native of Lu, registered in Jizhou; before I passed the examinations our prefecture had only one inspector and one revenue registrar, yet nothing was left undone.

sentences.zh: 自後有團練推官一人，太平興國中，增置通判、副使、判官、推官，而監酒、榷稅算又增四員。

translations.literal: Afterward there was one militia-training investigating officer; in Taiping Xingguo were added vice commissioner, deputy commissioner, judge, and investigating officer, and wine supervision, monopoly tax, and reckoning added four more posts.
translations.idiomatic: Later a militia-training investigating officer was added; in the Taiping Xingguo era came the vice commissioner, deputy, judge, and investigating officer, and wine supervision and tax monopoly offices added four more posts.

sentences.zh: 曹官之外，更益司理。

translations.literal: Beyond bureau officials, a judicial reviewer was further added.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the bureau staff, a judicial reviewer was added as well.

sentences.zh: 問其租稅，減於曩日也；

translations.literal: Ask about its land tax and levies—they are less than in former days;
translations.idiomatic: Ask about its tax revenue—it is less than before;

sentences.zh: 問其人民，逃於昔時也。

translations.literal: ask about its people—they have fled compared with former times.
translations.idiomatic: ask about its people—they have fled compared with earlier times.

sentences.zh: 一州既爾，天下可知。

translations.literal: If one prefecture is thus, all under Heaven may be known.
translations.idiomatic: If one prefecture is like this, the whole realm may be inferred.

sentences.zh: 冗吏耗於上，冗兵耗於下，此所以盡取山澤之利，而不能足也。

translations.literal: Redundant officials consume above, redundant troops consume below—this is why even taking all the profit of mountains and marshes cannot suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Redundant officials drain resources above and redundant troops below—that is why even exhausting the wealth of mountains and marshes cannot make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 夫山澤之利，與民共之。

translations.literal: The profit of mountains and marshes should be shared with the people.
translations.idiomatic: The wealth of mountains and marshes ought to be shared with the people.

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，取為國用，不可棄也；

translations.literal: Since the Han, they have been taken for state use and cannot be abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times, these revenues have been drawn for state use, and they cannot simply be abandoned;

sentences.zh: 然亦不可盡也。

translations.literal: yet neither can they be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: yet neither should they be exhausted to the last drop.

sentences.zh: 只如茶法，從古無稅，唐元和中，以用兵齊、蔡，始稅茶。

translations.literal: Take only the tea law—in antiquity there was no tax on tea; in the Yuanhe reign of Tang, to wage war against Qi and Cai, tea was first taxed.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the tea tax alone: from antiquity tea went untaxed, but in the Yuanhe era of the Tang, when troops were sent against Qi and Cai, taxation on tea was introduced for the first time.

sentences.zh: 《唐史》稱是歲得錢四十萬貫，今則數百萬矣，民何以堪？

translations.literal: The History of Tang says that year brought in four hundred thousand strings of cash; today it is several million—how can the people bear it?
translations.idiomatic: The History of Tang records that the levy brought in four hundred thousand strings of cash that year; today it runs to several million. How can the people endure it?

sentences.zh: 臣故曰減冗兵，併冗吏，使山澤之饒，稍流於下者此也。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore says that reducing redundant troops and consolidating redundant officials, so that the abundance of mountains and marshes may flow somewhat downward—this is that.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I again urge reducing redundant troops and consolidating redundant officials, so that some of the wealth of mountains and marshes may flow down to the people.

sentences.zh: 三曰艱難選舉，使入官不濫。

translations.literal: Third: make selection for office difficult, so that entry into office is not indiscriminate.
translations.idiomatic: Third, make the path to office difficult, so that appointment to office is not promiscuous.

sentences.zh: 古者鄉舉里選，為官擇人，士君子學行修於家，然後薦之朝廷，歷代雖有沿革，未嘗遠去其道。

translations.literal: In antiquity recommendation came through village and neighborhood selection; men were chosen for office, scholars and gentlemen cultivated learning and conduct at home, and only then were they recommended to court. Though dynasties had changes, they never departed far from this way.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity men were chosen through village recommendation and neighborhood selection: gentlemen cultivated learning and character at home before being recommended to the court. Though successive dynasties changed the system in detail, none ever strayed far from this principle.

sentences.zh: 隋、唐始有科試，太祖之世，每歲進士不過三十人，經學五十人。

translations.literal: Sui and Tang first had the examination system; in the time of Taizu, each year jinshi graduates did not exceed thirty, and classics graduates fifty.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui and Tang introduced civil examinations; in Taizu's reign only about thirty jinshi and fifty classics graduates passed each year.

sentences.zh: 重以諸侯不得奏辟，士大夫罕有資蔭，故有終身不獲一第，沒齒不獲一官者。

translations.literal: Moreover, regional lords were barred from submitting recommendations, and scholar-officials rarely had inherited privilege, so there were those who in a lifetime never attained one rank, or to the end of their teeth never gained one office.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, feudal lords could no longer recommend candidates by memorial, and few scholar-officials enjoyed hereditary privilege; some went their whole lives without passing an examination, or died without ever holding office.

sentences.zh: 太宗毓德王藩，睹其如此。

translations.literal: Taizong, while cultivating virtue in the princely fief, witnessed it thus.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizong was still a prince cultivating virtue in his fief, he saw this state of affairs.

sentences.zh: 臨御之後，不求備以取人，舍短用長，拔十得五。

translations.literal: After he ascended the throne, not seeking completeness in selecting men, setting aside the short and employing the long, of ten lifted five were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, he did not demand perfection in those he chose; he overlooked minor faults to use men's strengths, and of every ten candidates he raised, five proved worthy.

sentences.zh: 在位將逾二紀，登第殆近萬人，雖有俊傑之才，亦有容易而得。

translations.literal: On the throne for nearly two reign-periods, those who passed the examinations approached ten thousand; though there were outstanding talents, there were also those who obtained it easily.
translations.idiomatic: In nearly two decades on the throne, almost ten thousand men passed the examinations—among them were outstanding talents, but also many who had obtained degrees too easily.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為數百年之艱難，故先帝濟之以泛取，二十載之霈澤，陛下宜糾之以舊章，望以舉場還有司，如故事。

translations.literal: Your subject in foolishness considers that centuries of difficulty were therefore aided by the former emperor through broad selection; after twenty years of abundant grace, Your Majesty ought to rectify it by old regulations, hoping to return the examination grounds to the appropriate offices, as in former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe that centuries of scarcity were remedied by the former emperor's policy of broad recruitment; after twenty years of that generous indulgence, Your Majesty ought to restore the old rules and return control of the examinations to the proper agencies, as precedent dictates.

sentences.zh: 至於吏部銓官，亦非帝王躬親之事，自來五品已下，謂之旨授官，今幕職、州縣而已，京官雖有選限，多不施行。

translations.literal: As for the Ministry of Personnel's selection of officials, that too is not a matter for the emperor to attend to in person; from former times, those of fifth rank and below were called appointments by imperial order; today it applies only to secretariat staff and prefectural and district posts. Though metropolitan officials have selection terms, they are largely not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel's appointment of officials is likewise no business for the emperor to handle personally. From of old, posts of fifth rank and below were known as appointments by imperial order; today that means only secretarial and local posts. Though metropolitan officials have term limits on paper, they are seldom enforced.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜以吏部還有司，依格敕注擬可也。

translations.literal: Your subject in foolishness considers that the Ministry of Personnel ought to be returned to the appropriate offices, and appointments made according to regulations and edicts would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the Ministry of Personnel should likewise be left to the proper agencies, with appointments made according to the regulations and edicts.

sentences.zh: 四曰沙汰僧尼，使疲民無耗。

translations.literal: Fourth: sift out and eliminate monks and nuns, so that weary commoners suffer no drain.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, cull monks and nuns, so that the burdened populace is not further drained.

sentences.zh: 夫古者惟有四民，兵不在其數。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were only four classes of people; soldiers were not counted among them.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there were only four classes of people; the military was not counted as a separate class.

sentences.zh: 蓋古者井田之法，農即兵也。

translations.literal: For in antiquity under the well-field system, farmers were also soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Under the ancient well-field system, the farmer was also the soldier.

sentences.zh: 自秦以來，戰士不服農業，是四民之外，又生一民，故農益困。

translations.literal: Since Qin, warriors did not engage in agriculture; beyond the four classes another class was born, so farmers grew ever more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qin, warriors no longer worked the land—a fifth class arose beyond the four, and the burden on farmers grew heavier.

sentences.zh: 然執干戈衛社稷，理不可去。

translations.literal: Yet to take up weapons and guard the altars of soil and grain—in principle this cannot be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who bear arms to defend the realm cannot in principle be dispensed with.

sentences.zh: 漢明之後，佛法流入中國，度人修寺，歷代增加。

translations.literal: After Emperor Ming of Han, Buddhist dharma flowed into China; ordaining people and building temples increased through successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming of Han, Buddhism entered China; ordinations and temple-building multiplied with each dynasty.

sentences.zh: 不蠶而衣，不耕而食，是五民之外，又益一而為六矣。

translations.literal: Not rearing silkworms yet clothed, not plowing yet fed—these added one more beyond the five classes to make six.
translations.idiomatic: They wove no silk yet wore robes, tilled no fields yet ate grain—a sixth class beyond the five.
