sentences.zh: 假使天下有萬僧，日食米一升，歲用絹一匹，是至儉也，猶月費三千斛，歲用萬縑，何況五七萬輩哉。

translations.literal: Suppose all under Heaven had ten thousand monks, eating one sheng of rice daily and using one bolt of silk yearly—this would be extreme frugality—still monthly three thousand hu would be spent, yearly ten thousand bolts of silk; how much more with fifty or seventy thousand?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose the realm held ten thousand monks, each consuming a sheng of rice a day and a bolt of silk a year—the most Spartan allowance imaginable—still three thousand hu of grain per month and ten thousand bolts of silk per year would be consumed. What of fifty or seventy thousand monks?

sentences.zh: 不曰民蠹得乎？

translations.literal: Is it not rightly called a plague upon the people?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not plainly a drain upon the people?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為國家度人眾矣，造寺多矣，計其費耗，何啻億萬。

translations.literal: Your subject in foolishness considers that the state has ordained too many, built too many temples; calculating the cost, it is nothing less than hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the state has ordained too many monks and built too many temples; their cost runs to hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 先朝不豫，舍施又多，佛若有靈，豈不蒙福？

translations.literal: When the previous court was unwell, donations were also many; if Buddha has spiritual power, should he not have received blessing?
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor fell ill, still more donations were made; if the Buddha possessed spiritual power, would he not already have bestowed his blessing?

sentences.zh: 事佛無效，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Serving Buddha was ineffective—it can clearly be known.
translations.idiomatic: That worship of Buddha avails nothing is plainly evident.

sentences.zh: 願陛下深鑒治本，亟行沙汰，如以嗣位之初，未欲驚駭此輩，且可以二十載，不度人修寺，使自銷鑠，亦救弊之一端也

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty deeply to reflect on remedying the root, urgently to carry out winnowing and elimination; if in the first years of succeeding the throne you do not yet wish to startle this crowd, you may for twenty years forbid ordinations and temple-building, letting them wear away of themselves—this too is one means of remedying abuses.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will look to the root of the problem and act swiftly to cull their numbers. If you do not yet wish to alarm them at the start of your reign, forbid ordinations and new temples for twenty years and let the order dwindle on its own—that alone would be one remedy for this ill.

sentences.zh: 五曰親大臣，遠小人，使忠良蹇諤之士，知進而不疑，姦憸傾巧之徒，知退而有懼。

translations.literal: Fifth: be intimate with great ministers and keep petty men at a distance, so that loyal and worthy straight-speaking gentlemen know to advance without doubt, and wicked, sycophantic, scheming fellows know to withdraw with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, keep close to great ministers and hold petty men at arm's length, so that loyal and upright men know they may advance without fear, and the wicked, fawning, and scheming know they must retreat in dread.

sentences.zh: 夫君為元首，臣為股肱，言同體也。

translations.literal: The lord is the head, ministers are arms and legs—one speaks of a single body.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the head and ministers the limbs—they form one body.

sentences.zh: 得其人則勿疑，非其人則不用。

translations.literal: When you get the right man, do not doubt; when it is not the right man, do not use him.
translations.idiomatic: When the right man is found, do not doubt him; when the wrong man appears, do not employ him.

sentences.zh: 凡議帝王之盛者，豈不曰堯、舜之時，契作司徒，咎繇作士，伯夷典禮，后夔典樂，禹平水土，益作虞官。

translations.literal: Whenever one discusses the greatness of emperors and kings, does one not say that in the time of Yao and Shun, Qi was made Minister of Education, Gao Yao made Minister of Crime, Bo Yi managed rites, Hou Kui managed music, Yu levelled water and soil, and Yi became Superintendent of Forestry?
translations.idiomatic: Whoever speaks of an emperor's greatness invokes the age of Yao and Shun—when Qi served as Minister of Education, Gao Yao as Minister of Crime, Bo Yi overseer of rites, Hou Kui of music, Yu who tamed the floods, and Yi superintendent of forestry.

sentences.zh: 委任責成，而堯有知人任賢之德。

translations.literal: Entrusting responsibility and demanding achievement—thus Yao had the virtue of knowing men and employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Each was entrusted with responsibility and held accountable—and thus Yao earned his renown for discerning talent and putting the worthy to use.

sentences.zh: 雖然，堯之道遠矣，臣請以近事言之。

translations.literal: Even so, Yao's way is far removed; your subject requests to speak from recent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the way of Yao lies far in the past; let me speak from more recent history.

sentences.zh: 唐元和中，憲宗嘗命裴垍銓品庶官，垍曰：『天子擇宰相，宰相擇諸司長官，長官自擇僚屬，則上下不疑，而政成矣。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era of Tang, Emperor Xianzong once ordered Pei Ji to evaluate and rank common officials. Ji said: "The Son of Heaven chooses the chancellor; the chancellor chooses the directors of the various bureaus; directors choose their own subordinates—then above and below will not doubt, and governance will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, Emperor Xianzong once charged Pei Ji with rating officials of all ranks. Pei Ji said: "Let the Son of Heaven choose the chancellor; let the chancellor choose the bureau heads; let the heads choose their own staff—then there will be no suspicion between high and low, and governance will succeed."

sentences.zh: 』識者以垍為知言。

translations.literal: Those of discernment considered Ji one who spoke to the point.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment regarded Pei Ji as one who spoke wisely.

sentences.zh: 願陛下遠取帝堯，近鑒唐室，既得宰相，用而不疑。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty far to take Emperor Yao as model, near to mirror the Tang house; once you have obtained a chancellor, employ him without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will look back to Emperor Yao and take recent Tang history as a mirror: once you have found your chancellor, use him without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 使宰相擇諸司長官，長官自取僚屬，則垂拱而治矣。

translations.literal: Let the chancellor choose the bureau directors, and directors choose their own subordinates—then you may rule with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: Let the chancellor pick the bureau heads and the heads pick their own staff, and you may govern with hands folded in repose.

sentences.zh: 古者刑人不在君側，《語》曰：『放鄭聲，遠佞人。

translations.literal: In antiquity those who had suffered punishment were not at the ruler's side. The Analects says: "Banish the music of Zheng; keep petty men at a distance."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, men who had suffered punishment did not serve at the ruler's side. The Analects says: "Banish the licentious music of Zheng; keep sycophants at a distance."

sentences.zh: 』是以周文王左右，無可結襪者，言皆賢也。

translations.literal: Therefore at King Wen of Zhou's left and right there was no one fit only to tie socks—all were worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Hence at King Wen of Zhou's side there was no one whose talents ran only to tying socks—every man near him was worthy.

sentences.zh: 夫小人巧言令色，先意希旨，事必害正，心惟忌賢，非聖明不能深察。

translations.literal: Petty men have clever words and pleasing countenance, anticipate intent and seek to please; their affairs necessarily harm the upright, their hearts only envy the worthy—unless one is sage-like and enlightened, one cannot thoroughly discern them.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men speak cleverly and look pleasant; they anticipate the ruler's wishes and seek to flatter. Their deeds inevitably harm the upright, and their hearts are consumed with envy of the worthy—only a sage ruler can see through them.

sentences.zh: 舊制，南班三品，尚書方得升殿；

translations.literal: By old regulation, among the Southern Rank, only at third rank could a Director rise to the hall audience;
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, among officials of the Southern Rank, only those of Director rank and above were permitted to ascend to the imperial hall;

sentences.zh: 比來三班奉職，或因遣使，亦許升殿，惑亂天聽，無甚於此。

translations.literal: Recently, attendants of the third class of the three ranks, sometimes because of dispatch on missions, were also allowed to ascend the hall—confusing the Heavenly Ears, nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Recently even attendants of the third rank of the three classes, merely because they had been sent on errands, have been allowed into the hall—nothing confuses the imperial ear more than this.

sentences.zh: 願陛下振舉紀綱，尊嚴視聽，在此時矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to rouse and uphold discipline, dignify sight and hearing—the time is now.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will restore discipline and dignity to what reaches your eyes and ears—now is the moment.

sentences.zh: 臣愚又以為今之所急，在先議兵，使眾寡得其宜，措置得其道。

translations.literal: Your subject in foolishness further considers that what is urgent now is first to discuss troops, so that numbers fit what is fitting and arrangements follow the right way.
translations.idiomatic: I further believe that what is most urgent today is to address the military first—so that force is sized appropriately and deployed rightly.

sentences.zh: 然後議吏，使清濁殊塗，品流不雜，然後艱選舉以塞其源，禁僧尼以去其耗，自然國用足而王道行矣。」

translations.literal: Then discuss officials, so that pure and turbid follow separate paths and ranks are not mixed; then make selection difficult to block its source and forbid monks and nuns to remove their drain—naturally state revenue will suffice and the royal way will prevail."
translations.idiomatic: Then address officialdom, so that the worthy and the unworthy travel separate paths and ranks are kept pure; then tighten examinations to choke off abuse at the source and restrict monks and nuns to remove the drain. State revenue will naturally suffice and the royal way will prevail."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，召還，復知制誥。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was recalled and again made Drafting Officer for Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he was recalled and restored to his post as Drafting Officer for Edicts.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，預修《太祖實錄》，直書其事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Taizu, writing events straightforwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping era he helped compile the Veritable Records of Taizu, recording events without evasion.

sentences.zh: 時宰相張齊賢、李沆不協，意禹偁議論輕重其間。

translations.literal: At the time the chancellors Zhang Qixian and Li Hang were at odds; they believed Yucheng's comments favored one side over the other.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors Zhang Qixian and Li Hang were then at odds, and they suspected Yucheng's judgments in the record had tipped the balance between them.

sentences.zh: 出知黃州，嘗作《三黜賦》以見志。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Huangzhou; he once wrote the "Rhapsody on Three Dismissals" to express his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as prefect of Huangzhou, where he wrote the "Rhapsody on Three Dismissals" to declare his convictions.

sentences.zh: 其卒章云：「屈於身而不屈於道兮，雖百謫而何虧！」

translations.literal: Its closing passage says: "Bending in body yet not bending in the Way—though demoted a hundred times, what is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Its closing lines read: "The body may bow, but the Way will not—though banished a hundred times, what have I lost?"

sentences.zh: 三年，濮州盜夜入城，略知州王守信、監軍王昭度，禹偁聞而奏疏，略曰：「伏以體國經野，王者保邦之制也。

translations.literal: In the third year, bandits at night entered the city of Puzhou, abducted the prefect Wang Shouxin and the army supervisor Wang Zhaodu; Yucheng heard and submitted a memorial, summarizing: "Your subject considers that organizing the state and governing the fields is the system by which a king preserves the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In his third year there, bandits broke into Puzhou by night and carried off Prefect Wang Shouxin and Army Supervisor Wang Zhaodu. On hearing this, Yucheng submitted a memorial that began: "Your subject submits that organizing the state and governing the realm is the sovereign's means of securing the country.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：『王公設險，以守其國。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Kings and dukes set up defenses to guard their states."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Kings and dukes establish defenses to guard their domains."

sentences.zh: 』自五季亂離，各據城壘，豆分瓜剖，七十餘年。

translations.literal: Since the disorder and separation of the Five Dynasties, each held walled strongholds, split like beans or melons—more than seventy years.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos of the Five Dynasties, when each warlord held his own fortress and the land was carved up like beans in a dish, more than seventy years have passed.

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗，削平僭偽，天下一家。

translations.literal: Taizu and Taizong cut down the usurpations and false regimes; all under Heaven became one house.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Taizong suppressed the usurpers and reunified the realm.

sentences.zh: 當時議者，乃令江淮諸郡毀城隍、收兵甲、徹武備者，二十餘年。

translations.literal: The advisers of that time then had the commanderies of Jiang and Huai destroy their walls and moats, collect weapons and armor, and dismantle military preparations—for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: The policy advisers of that day ordered the Jiang and Huai prefectures to dismantle city walls, collect weapons, and strip defenses—a policy pursued for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 書生領州，大郡給二十人，小郡減五人，以充常從。

translations.literal: Scholars led prefectures; large prefectures were given twenty men, small ones five fewer, to serve as regular attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials governed the prefectures; large ones received twenty retainers, smaller ones fifteen, to serve as regular attendants.

sentences.zh: 號曰長吏，實同旅人；

translations.literal: Called prefectural magistrates, they were in reality like travelers;
translations.idiomatic: In name they were prefectural magistrates; in fact they were little more than passers-through;

sentences.zh: 名為郡城，蕩若平地。

translations.literal: in name they were commandery cities, open as level ground.
translations.idiomatic: in name they were walled cities; in truth they lay open as flat fields.

sentences.zh: 雖則尊京師而抑郡縣，為強幹弱枝之術，亦匪得其中道也。

translations.literal: Although this honored the capital and suppressed commanderies and counties, as the technique of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches, it also did not hit the middle way.
translations.idiomatic: Though this elevated the capital at the expense of the prefectures—the classic "strong trunk, weak branches" strategy—it missed the middle path.

sentences.zh: 臣比在滁州，值發兵挽漕，關城無人守禦，止以白直代主開閉，城池頹圮，鎧仗不完。

translations.literal: Your subject recently was at Chuzhou; when troops were dispatched for transport, the barrier city had no one to guard and defend—a raw conscript simply substituted to open and close the gates; walls and moats crumbled, armor and weapons were incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: When I was at Chuzhou, troops were conscripted for grain transport, leaving the city gates unmanned; raw recruits merely opened and closed them. The walls crumbled and armor and weapons lay in disrepair.

sentences.zh: 及徙維揚，稱為重鎮，乃與滁州無異。

translations.literal: When transferred to Weiyang, called a key strongpoint, it was no different from Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When I was transferred to Yangzhou, though it was considered a major stronghold, conditions were no different from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗出鎧甲三十副，與巡警使臣，彀弩張弓，十損四五，蓋不敢擅有修治，上下因循，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Once thirty suits of armor were issued to the patrol commissioner; when cocking crossbows and drawing bows, four or five of ten were damaged—for fear of unauthorized repair, above and below drifted along, until it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: I once issued thirty suits of armor to a patrol commissioner; when his men tried to cock crossbows and draw bows, four or five in ten failed. No one dared repair equipment without authorization, and complacency at every level had brought things to this pass.

sentences.zh: 今黃州城雉器甲，復不及滁、揚。

translations.literal: Now Huangzhou's battlements and weapons and armor again do not reach those of Chuzhou and Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Today at Huangzhou, walls and armor are in even worse shape than at Chuzhou or Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬一水旱為災，盜賊竊發，雖思禦備，何以枝梧。

translations.literal: If by chance flood or drought brings disaster, or bandits steal forth, though one wishes to prepare defense, with what will one resist?
translations.idiomatic: Should flood or drought strike, or bandits rise, even the will to defend would avail nothing—what could be done to resist?

sentences.zh: 蓋太祖削諸侯跋扈之勢，太宗杜僭偽覬望之心，不得不爾。

translations.literal: Taizu cut down the overbearing power of feudal lords; Taizong blocked the covetous hearts of usurpers and false regimes—they had no choice but to do thus.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had to curb the overweening power of regional lords; Taizong had to suppress the lingering ambitions of the old usurpers. Circumstances left them no choice.

sentences.zh: 其如設法救世，久則弊生，救弊之道，在乎從宜。

translations.literal: Yet as establishing laws to save the age—long maintained, abuses arise; the way to remedy abuses lies in adapting to what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet laws made to save the age, maintained too long, breed new abuses; the remedy lies in adapting to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 疾若轉規，固不可膠柱而鼓瑟也。

translations.literal: Swift as turning a compass, one certainly cannot tune the zither by gluing the pegs.
translations.idiomatic: Change must come as swiftly as a wheel's turn; one cannot play the zither with pegs glued in place.

sentences.zh: 今江、淮諸州，大患有三：城池墮圮，一也；

translations.literal: Now among the prefectures of Jiang and Huai, great ills have three: walls and moats collapsing—first;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang and Huai prefectures suffer three grave ills: first, crumbling walls and moats;

sentences.zh: 兵仗不完，二也；

translations.literal: weapons and armor incomplete—second;
translations.idiomatic: second, deficient weapons and armor;

sentences.zh: 軍不服習，三也；

translations.literal: troops not practiced in drill—third;
translations.idiomatic: third, troops untrained for war.

sentences.zh: 濮賊之興，慢防可見。

translations.literal: The rise of the Puzhou bandits—neglect of defense is plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: The Puzhou incident shows plainly where lax defense leads.

sentences.zh: 望陛下特紆宸斷，許江、淮諸郡，酌民戶眾寡，城池大小，並置守捉。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty especially will extend imperial decision, permitting the commanderies of Jiang and Huai, according to the multitude or fewness of households and the size of cities, all to establish garrison guards.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will deign to authorize each Jiang and Huai prefecture, according to its population and the size of its walls, to establish garrison forces.

sentences.zh: 軍士多不過五百人，閱習弓劍，然後漸葺城壁，繕完甲胄，則郡國有禦侮之備，長吏免剽略之虞矣。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers mostly not exceeding five hundred men, drilling with bow and sword; then gradually repair walls, complete armor and helmets—then commanderies and states will have preparations against insult, and prefectural magistrates will be spared anxiety of plunder and abduction.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons need be no larger than five hundred men, trained in bow and sword; walls can then be gradually repaired and armor restored—giving the prefectures the means to repel attack and sparing their magistrates the fear of abduction.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted and the emperor approved it with praise.

sentences.zh: 四年，州境二虎鬥，其一死，食之殆半。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, two tigers fought within the prefecture borders; one died, and nearly half was eaten.
translations.idiomatic: In his fourth year there, two tigers fought within the prefecture; one was killed and nearly half its body consumed.

sentences.zh: 群雞夜鳴，經月不止。

translations.literal: Flocks of roosters crowed at night, unceasing for a month.
translations.idiomatic: Flocks of roosters crowed through the night, unabated for a full month.

sentences.zh: 冬雷暴作。

translations.literal: In winter thunder burst forth.
translations.idiomatic: Winter brought violent thunderstorms.

sentences.zh: 禹偁手疏引《洪範傳》陳戒，且自劾；

translations.literal: Yucheng by personal memorial cited the Commentary on the Hong Fan to offer warnings, and also impeached himself;
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng submitted a personal memorial citing the Commentary on the Hong Fan to set forth omens as warnings, and impeached himself as well;

sentences.zh: 上遣內侍乘驛勞問，醮禳之，詢日官，云：「守土者當其咎。

translations.literal: the emperor sent a palace attendant by post relay to comfort and inquire, performed Daoist rites of exorcism, and asked the calendar officials, who said: "Those who guard the soil bear the blame."
translations.idiomatic: the emperor sent a palace attendant by express relay to inquire after him and ordered exorcistic rites. When he consulted the calendar officials, they said: "The blame falls on the official who holds the land."

sentences.zh: 」上惜禹偁才，是日，命徙蘄州。

translations.literal: The emperor valued Yucheng's talent; that same day he ordered him transferred to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued Yucheng's talent, and that same day ordered his transfer to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 禹偁上表謝，有「宣室鬼神之問，不望生還；

translations.literal: Yucheng submitted a thank-you memorial, containing the phrases "the questioning of ghosts and spirits in the Xuan Room—I do not expect to return alive;
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng submitted a memorial of thanks containing the lines "Like the questioning of ghost and spirit in the Xuan Room, I expect no return to life;

sentences.zh: 茂陵封禪之書，止期身後」之語。

translations.literal: the fengshan book at Maoling—only expected after death"—such language.
translations.idiomatic: Like the fengshan memorial at Maoling, destined only for after my death."

sentences.zh: 上異之，果至郡未逾月而卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: The emperor found it strange; sure enough, he reached the prefecture not more than a month before he died, age forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by this, and indeed Yucheng died less than a month after reaching his new post, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，甚悼之，厚賻其家。

translations.literal: When death was reported, he greatly mourned him and richly compensated his family.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death arrived, the emperor mourned him deeply and granted his family a generous award.

sentences.zh: 賜一子出身。

translations.literal: He granted one son entry into office by qualification.
translations.idiomatic: He granted one of his sons qualification for office.

sentences.zh: 禹偁詞學敏贍，遇事敢言，喜臧否人物，以直躬行道為己任。

translations.literal: Yucheng was quick and rich in literary composition, dared to speak when matters arose, delighted in judging persons good and bad, and took straight conduct and practicing the Way as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Yucheng was a fluent and prolific writer who spoke boldly when occasion demanded, delighted in appraising the character of others, and held integrity and moral rectitude as his personal duty.

sentences.zh: 嘗云：「吾若生元和時，從事於李絳、崔群間，斯無愧矣。

translations.literal: He once said: "If I had been born in the Yuanhe era and served among Li Jiang and Cui Qun, I would have no shame."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Had I lived in the Yuanhe era and served alongside Li Jiang and Cui Qun, I would have nothing to regret."

sentences.zh: 」其為文著書，多涉規諷，以是頗為流俗所不容，故屢見擯斥。

translations.literal: His writings and books mostly touched on admonition and satire; for this he was rather not tolerated by vulgar custom, and therefore was repeatedly driven out.
translations.idiomatic: His essays and books were largely satirical and admonitory; conventional society could not abide him, and he was repeatedly cast aside.

sentences.zh: 所與遊必儒雅，後進有詞藝者，極意稱揚之。

translations.literal: Those with whom he associated were invariably refined and learned; for junior fellows with literary talent, he exhaustively praised and promoted them.
translations.idiomatic: He associated only with learned and cultivated men, and praised aspiring writers to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 如孫何、丁謂輩，多遊其門。

translations.literal: Such as Sun He, Ding Wei, and the like—many moved within his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He, Ding Wei, and others of that generation often gathered at his door.

sentences.zh: 有《小畜集》二十卷、《承明集》十卷、《集議》十卷、詩三卷。

translations.literal: He had the Collection of Small Accumulations in twenty scrolls, the Chenming Collection in ten scrolls, the Collected Discussions in ten scrolls, and poetry in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left behind the Collection of Small Accumulations in twenty scrolls, the Chenming Collection in ten, the Collected Discussions in ten, and three scrolls of poetry.

sentences.zh: 子嘉祐、嘉言俱知名。

translations.literal: His sons Jiayou and Jiayan were both renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jiayou and Jiayan both achieved renown.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐為館職，寇準曰：「吾尹京，外議云何？

translations.literal: Jiayou held a post in the Academy; Kou Zhun said: "I govern the capital—what does outside opinion say?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou held a post in the Hanlin Academy. Kou Zhun asked him: "I am governing the capital—what are people saying outside?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「人言丈人且入相。

translations.literal: He replied: "People say my elder is about to enter the chancellorship."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "People say you are about to become chancellor."

sentences.zh: 」準曰：「於吾子意何如？

translations.literal: Zhun said: "In your opinion, what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun asked: "What is your view of that?"

sentences.zh: 」嘉祐曰：「以愚觀之，不若不為相之善也，相則譽望損矣。

translations.literal: Jiayou said: "In your subject's foolish view, it would be better not to become chancellor; as chancellor, reputation and standing would be diminished."
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou said: "In my humble judgment, it would be better if you did not take the post. Chancellor would diminish your standing."

sentences.zh: 自古賢相，所以能建功業、澤生民者，其君臣相得，如魚之有水，故言聽計從，而臣主俱榮。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, the reason worthy chancellors could achieve merit and benefit the living people was that ruler and minister matched each other like fish has water; therefore words were heeded and plans followed, and minister and lord both gained glory.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history great chancellors have achieved lasting work and served the people because ruler and minister harmonized like fish and water—counsel was heeded, plans followed, and both prospered.

sentences.zh: 今丈人負天下重望，中外有太平之責焉，丈人於明主，能若魚之有水乎？

translations.literal: Now my elder bears heavy reputation under Heaven; within and without there is responsibility for great peace—can my elder with the enlightened lord be like fish has water?
translations.idiomatic: You bear the highest reputation in the realm, and both court and country look to you for peace. With this enlightened sovereign, can you truly be like fish in water?

sentences.zh: 」準大喜，執其手曰：「元之雖文章冠天下，至於深識遠慮，或不逮吾子也。

translations.literal: Zhun greatly rejoiced, grasped his hand, and said: "Although Yuanzhi's literary works crown all under Heaven, as for deep insight and far-sighted consideration, perhaps he does not reach my son."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was delighted and took his hand. "Though Yuanzhi's prose tops the realm, in depth of insight and breadth of vision he may not match you."

sentences.zh: 」嘉祐官不顯。

translations.literal: "Jiayou's official rank was not illustrious."
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou's official career never rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 嘉言以進士第為江都簿，真宗嘗觀禹偁奏章，嗟美切直，因訪其後，宰相以嘉言聞。

translations.literal: Jiayan, having passed the jinshi examination, served as clerk of Jiangdu. Emperor Zhenzong once viewed Wang Yucheng's memorials, sighed in admiration of their blunt directness, and inquiring about his descendants, the chancellor reported Jiayan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayan, a jinshi graduate, served as clerk of Jiangdu. When Zhenzong read Wang Yucheng's memorials and admired their forthright candor, he asked who had succeeded him; the chancellor named Jiayan.

sentences.zh: 即召對，擢大理評事，至殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was immediately summoned for audience, promoted to Assistant Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review, and advanced to Attendant Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately called to court, made Assistant Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review, and eventually Attendant Censor within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 曾孫汾舉進士甲科，仕至工部侍郎，入元祐黨籍。

translations.literal: His great-grandson Fen passed the jinshi examination in the top grade, served to Vice Minister of Works, and was entered on the Yuanyou faction register.
translations.idiomatic: A great-grandson, Fen, earned top honors on the jinshi examination, rose to Vice Minister of Works, and was later listed among the Yuanyou partisans.

sentences.zh: 張詠，字復之，濮州鄄城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong, style name Fuzhi, was a man of Juancheng in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong, courtesy name Fuzhi, was a native of Juancheng in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少任氣，不拘小節，雖貧賤客遊，未嘗下人。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold-spirited and unconstrained by petty etiquette; though poor and wandering as a guest, he never deferred to others.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was spirited and scorned small proprieties; even when poor and traveling far from home, he never humbled himself before others.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，郡舉進士，議以詠首薦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo the prefecture recommended candidates for the jinshi examination, and the discussion was to recommend Yong first.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, when the prefecture put forward jinshi candidates, the plan was to recommend Yong at the head of the list.

sentences.zh: 有夙儒張覃者未第，詠與寇準致書郡將，薦覃為首，眾許其能讓。

translations.literal: There was an elder scholar named Zhang Tan who had not yet passed the examination; Yong and Kou Zhun wrote to the prefectural commander recommending Tan first, and all praised Yong's capacity to yield.
translations.idiomatic: An elderly scholar, Zhang Tan, had repeatedly failed the examinations; Yong and Kou Zhun wrote the prefectural commander urging that Tan be placed first, and everyone admired Yong's willingness to stand aside.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詠登進士乙科，大理評事、知鄂州崇陽縣。

translations.literal: That year Yong passed the jinshi examination in the second grade, was made Assistant Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review, and appointed magistrate of Chongyang County in E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yong passed the jinshi examination in the second tier and was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Chongyang County in E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 再遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Assistant Academician of Writings.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Assistant Academician of Writings.

sentences.zh: 以蘇易簡薦，入為太子中允，遷秘書丞、通判麟相二州，乞掌濮州市征以便養。

translations.literal: On Su Yijian's recommendation he entered the capital as Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent, was transferred to Secretariat Director and Vice-Prefect of Lin and Xiang Prefectures, and requested charge of the market tolls of Pu Prefecture so as to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Su Yijian, he was summoned to court as Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent, then made Secretariat Director and Vice-Prefect of Lin and Xiang Prefectures; he asked to administer the market taxes of Pu Prefecture so he could care for his parents nearby.

sentences.zh: 俄召還，賜緋魚，知浚儀縣。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled, granted the scarlet fish tally, and made magistrate of Junyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to the capital, granted the scarlet fish tally of a higher-ranking official, and appointed magistrate of Junyi County.

sentences.zh: 會李沆、宋湜、寇準連薦其才，以為荊湖北路轉運使，奏罷歸、峽二州水遞夫，就轉太常博士。

translations.literal: When Li Hang, Song Mo, and Kou Zhun successively recommended his talent, he was made Transport Intendant of the Jinghu North Circuit; he memorialized to abolish the water courier laborers of Gui and Xia Prefectures, and was then transferred to Academician Expositor of the Five Classics in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hang, Song Mo, and Kou Zhun then recommended him in succession, and he was appointed Transport Intendant of the Jinghu North Circuit. He memorialized to abolish the water courier corvée in Gui and Xia Prefectures and was soon transferred to Academician Expositor of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其強幹，召還，超拜虞部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong heard of his strong capability, recalled him, and by extraordinary promotion made him Director of the Bureau of Revenues, granting him gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, hearing of his exceptional competence, recalled him and skipped the usual steps to appoint him Director of the Bureau of Revenues, granting him the gold seal and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 旬日，與向敏中並擢為樞密直學士、同知銀臺台通進封駁司兼掌三班院。

translations.literal: Within ten days he and Xiang Minzhong were together promoted to Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council, Associate Director of the Silver Terrace Office for Memorial Transmission and Review, and concurrently in charge of the Three Classes Court.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he and Xiang Minzhong were both elevated to Hanlin Academicians of the Privy Council, made Associate Directors of the Silver Terrace Office for Memorial Transmission and Review, and put jointly in charge of the Three Classes Court.

sentences.zh: 張永德為幷代部署，有小校犯法，笞之至死，詔案其罪。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde was commander of the Bing and Dai deployment; a petty officer violated the law and was flogged to death, and an edict was issued to investigate the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde held command over Bing and Dai; a junior officer broke the law and was beaten to death, and the throne ordered an inquiry into the offense.

sentences.zh: 詠封還詔書，且言：「陛下方委永德邊任，若以一部校故，推辱主帥，臣恐下有輕上之心。

translations.literal: Yong sealed and returned the edict, saying: "Your Majesty has just entrusted Yongde with frontier command; if for the sake of one petty officer you humiliate the commander-in-chief, I fear those below will come to hold the sovereign lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Yong sealed the edict and sent it back, writing: "Your Majesty has only just entrusted Yongde with frontier command. To disgrace the commanding general over one junior officer, I fear, will teach the ranks below to hold their sovereign cheaply."

sentences.zh: 」太宗不從。

translations.literal: Taizong did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong would not be persuaded.

sentences.zh: 未幾，果有營兵脅訴軍校者，詠引前事為言，太宗改容勞之。

translations.literal: Before long, camp soldiers indeed coerced one another into bringing suits against army officers; Yong cited the earlier affair in explanation, and Taizong changed expression and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, garrison troops did in fact band together to bring suits against their officers. Yong invoked the earlier case, and Taizong's face softened as he praised him.

sentences.zh: 出知益州，時李順構亂，王繼恩、上官正總兵攻討，頓師不進。

translations.literal: He was sent out to govern Yizhou. At that time Li Shun had raised rebellion; Wang Jien and Shangguan Zheng commanded troops to attack and suppress it, but halted the army and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Yizhou. Li Shun had risen in rebellion, and though Wang Jien and Shangguan Zheng commanded the punitive force, the army stalled and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 詠以言激正，勉其親行，仍盛為供帳餞之。

translations.literal: Yong used words to rouse Zheng, urged him to go in person, and still set out a lavish farewell feast for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong goaded Zheng with sharp words, pressed him to lead the advance in person, and staged an elaborate farewell banquet in his honor.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，舉爵屬軍校曰：「汝曹蒙國厚恩，無以塞責，此行當直抵寇壘，平蕩醜類。

translations.literal: When the wine had warmed them, he raised his cup and addressed the army officers, saying: "You have received the state's deep grace and have no way to fulfill your duty; on this march you should strike straight at the rebel strongholds and sweep away the wicked host."
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was flowing, he raised his cup to the officers and said: "You owe the state a heavy debt of grace and have yet to repay it. This campaign must carry you straight to the rebel camps and wipe the enemy out."

sentences.zh: 若老師曠日，即此地還為爾死所矣。

translations.literal: If the army idles day after day, this very place will become your place of death in return.
translations.idiomatic: If you drag the campaign out day after day, this very ground will become the place where you die.

sentences.zh: 」正由是決行深入，大致克捷。

translations.literal: Zheng thereby resolved to march deep, and broadly achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng took this to heart, marched deep into enemy territory, and won a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 繼恩帳下卒縋城夜遁，吏執以告。

translations.literal: A soldier under Jien's command lowered himself from the wall and fled by night; officials seized him and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: One of Jien's men lowered himself over the wall and fled by night; the local officers caught him and reported the escape.

sentences.zh: 詠不欲與繼恩失歡，即命縶投眢井，人無知者。

translations.literal: Yong did not wish to fall out with Jien, so he immediately ordered the man bound and cast into an abandoned well, and no one knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to offend Jien, Yong had the man bound and thrown down an abandoned well, and no one was the wiser.

sentences.zh: 時寇略之際，民多脅從，詠移文諭以朝廷恩信，使各歸田里。

translations.literal: At a time when bandits were raiding, many common people had been coerced into following them; Yong issued a proclamation explaining the court's grace and good faith, causing each to return to field and village.
translations.idiomatic: While rebels were marauding, many people had been forced to join them; Yong issued a proclamation invoking the court's mercy and trustworthiness and sent them back to their farms and homes.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「前日李順脅民為賊，今日吾化賊為民，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: He also said: "Yesterday Li Shun forced the people to become bandits; today I transform bandits into people—is that not also fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Yesterday Li Shun forced the people into rebellion; today I am turning rebels back into subjects. Is that not fitting?"

sentences.zh: 」時民間訛言，有白頭翁午後食人兒女，一郡囂然。

translations.literal: At that time a false rumor spread among the people that a white-haired old man ate people's sons and daughters in the afternoon, and the whole prefecture was in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: A wild rumor then swept the countryside that a white-haired old man was devouring children in the afternoon, and the whole prefecture erupted in panic.

sentences.zh: 至暮，路無行人，既而得造訛者戮之，民遂帖息。

translations.literal: By evening there were no travelers on the roads; eventually the originator of the rumor was seized and executed, and the people then settled down.
translations.idiomatic: By evening the roads were empty; once the rumor-monger was found and executed, the people calmed down.

sentences.zh: 詠曰：「妖訛之興，沴氣乘之，妖則有形，訛則有聲，止訛之術，在乎識斷，不在乎厭勝也。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "When demonic rumors arise, pestilential qi rides upon them; demons have form, rumors have sound. The art of stopping rumors lies in discernment and decision, not in exorcistic victory."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said: "When strange rumors arise, they feed on the mood of the times. Omens take visible form; rumors take audible shape. The way to stop them is clear judgment, not charms and exorcisms."

sentences.zh: 初，蜀士知向學，而不樂仕宦。

translations.literal: At first the scholars of Shu knew to turn toward learning, yet did not delight in official careers.
translations.idiomatic: At first the scholars of Shu valued learning but had little taste for public office.

sentences.zh: 詠察郡人張及、李畋、張逵者皆有學行，為鄉里所稱；

translations.literal: Yong observed that Zhang Ji, Li Tian, and Zhang Kui, men of the prefecture, all possessed learning and conduct and were praised in their home districts;
translations.idiomatic: Yong noticed that three local men—Zhang Ji, Li Tian, and Zhang Kui—were learned and upright and widely respected in their communities;

sentences.zh: 遂敦勉就舉，而三人者悉登科，士由是知勸。

translations.literal: he therefore earnestly urged them to enter the examinations, and all three passed; scholars thereby knew encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: he earnestly urged them to sit for the examinations, and all three passed; from then on local scholars took the cue.

sentences.zh: 民有諜訴者，詠灼見情偽，立為判決，人皆厭服。

translations.literal: When the people brought espionage lawsuits, Yong clearly saw truth and falsehood and immediately rendered judgment; all submitted in satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: When people brought accusations of espionage, Yong saw through the truth at once, ruled on the spot, and left everyone convinced.

sentences.zh: 好事者編集其辭，鏤板傳布。

translations.literal: Enthusiasts compiled his written judgments, carved them on blocks, and circulated them.
translations.idiomatic: Admirers collected his rulings, had them carved on printing blocks, and circulated them widely.

sentences.zh: 詠嘗曰：「詢君子得君子，詢小人得小人，各就其黨詢之，則無不審矣。

translations.literal: Yong once said: "Inquire of gentlemen and you get gentlemen; inquire of petty men and you get petty men. Inquire each among his own faction, and nothing will fail to be scrutinized."
translations.idiomatic: Yong once said: "Ask gentlemen and you hear from gentlemen; ask petty men and you hear from petty men. Question each side among its own kind, and the truth will out every time."

sentences.zh: 」其為政，恩威並用，蜀民畏而愛之。

translations.literal: In his governance he employed grace and severity together; the people of Shu feared yet loved him.
translations.idiomatic: In governing he combined mercy with force, and the people of Shu feared him even as they loved him.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，起復，改兵部郎中。

translations.literal: On completing mourning for his father, he was recalled from mourning and changed to Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he entered mourning, but was recalled before it ended and made Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 會詔川、陝諸州參用銅鐵錢，每銅錢一當鐵錢十。

translations.literal: An edict came down that the prefectures of Sichuan and Shaanxi should jointly use copper and iron coin, with each copper coin equal to ten iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered the Sichuan and Shaanxi prefectures to use copper and iron coin side by side, fixing the rate at one copper coin to ten iron coins.

sentences.zh: 詠上言：「昨經利州，以銅錢一換鐵錢五，綿州銅錢一換鐵錢六，益州銅錢一換鐵錢八。

translations.literal: Yong submitted a memorial saying: "Yesterday passing through Lizhou, one copper coin exchanged for five iron coins; in Mianzhou one copper coin exchanged for six iron coins; in Yizhou one copper coin exchanged for eight iron coins."
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized the throne: "On my recent route through Lizhou, one copper coin fetched five iron coins; in Mianzhou, six; in Yizhou, eight."

sentences.zh: 若一其法，公私非便。

translations.literal: If the law is made uniform, it will be inconvenient for public and private interests alike.
translations.idiomatic: A single fixed rate would work hardship on both the government and the people.

sentences.zh: 望依旬估折納銅錢。」

translations.literal: "I hope copper coins may be collected according to the ten-day market estimate."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask that copper payments be assessed according to the prevailing ten-day market rate."

sentences.zh: 五年，馬知節自益徙延州，朝議擇可代者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ma Zhijie was transferred from Yizhou to Yanzhou, and the court deliberated on who could replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Ma Zhijie was moved from Yizhou to Yanzhou, and the court debated who should succeed him.

sentences.zh: 真宗以詠前在蜀治行優異，復命知益州，仍加刑部侍郎、樞密直學士，就遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, because Yong's earlier governance in Shu had been outstanding, again appointed him to govern Yizhou, additionally making him Vice Minister of Justice and Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council, and at the same time promoting him to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong, remembering Yong's distinguished record in Shu, sent him back to govern Yizhou, added the titles Vice Minister of Justice and Hanlin Academician of the Privy Council, and promoted him to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 轉運使黃觀上其治狀，有詔褒美。

translations.literal: Transport Intendant Huang Guan submitted a report on his governance, and an edict was issued praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Intendant Huang Guan reported on his administration, and the throne issued a decree of commendation.

sentences.zh: 會遣謝濤巡撫西蜀，上因令傳諭詠曰：「得卿在蜀，朕無西顧之憂矣。

translations.literal: When Xie Tao was dispatched to inspect and pacify western Shu, the emperor therefore had him relay to Yong, saying: "With you obtained in Shu, I have no worry for the west."
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Tao was sent to inspect western Shu, the emperor asked him to tell Yong: "With you in Shu, I need not look over my shoulder to the west."

sentences.zh: 」歸朝，復掌三班，領登聞檢院。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he again took charge of the Three Classes Court and headed the Dengwen Inspection Court.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court, he again managed the Three Classes Court and headed the Dengwen Inspection Court.

sentences.zh: 詠中歲瘍生腦，頗妨巾櫛，求知潁州。

translations.literal: In middle age a sore arose on Yong's head that greatly hindered his grooming; he requested appointment to Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In middle age a festering sore on his head made grooming painful, and he asked to be sent to Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗以其公直，有時望，再任益部，皆以政績聞，不當蒞小郡。

translations.literal: Zhenzong, because he was upright and enjoyed reputation in his time, and because both times he had governed the Yi region his achievements were renowned, held that he ought not take a small prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong considered him upright, widely respected, and proven in two terms governing Shu; a minor prefecture was beneath him.

sentences.zh: 令中書召問，將委以青杜或真定，令其自擇。

translations.literal: He ordered the Secretariat to summon and question him, intending to entrust him with Qing Prefecture or Zhending, and let him choose for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Secretariat to summon Yong and offer him either Qingzhou or Zhending, letting him choose.

sentences.zh: 詠辭不就，遂命知昇州。

translations.literal: Yong declined and would not accept; he was therefore appointed to govern Sheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yong declined both posts, and was instead appointed prefect of Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，加左丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was given the additional title of Left Assistant Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era he was made Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年春，州民以詠秩滿借留，就轉工部尚書，令再任。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the people of the prefecture, because Yong's term was complete, petitioned to retain him; he was thereupon transferred to Minister of Works and ordered to serve another term.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the people petitioned to keep him when his term expired; he was promoted to Minister of Works and asked to stay on.

sentences.zh: 是秋，以江左旱歉，命充昇、宣等十州安撫使，進禮部。

translations.literal: That autumn, because of drought and famine south of the Yangtze, he was appointed Commissioner to Pacify Sheng, Xuan, and nine other prefectures, and was advanced to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, drought and famine struck the lower Yangtze region, and he was made Pacification Commissioner for Sheng, Xuan, and eight other prefectures while being promoted to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上聞詠腦瘍甚，憫之，令薛映馳驛代還。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Yong's head sore was severe, pitied him, and ordered Xue Ying to ride post-horses and replace him so he could return.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned how badly Yong's head ailment had worsened, he took pity on him and sent Xue Ying by express relay to relieve him and bring him home.

sentences.zh: 以疾未見，恨不得面陳所蘊，乃抗論言：「近年虛國帑藏，竭生民膏血，以奉無用之土木，皆賊臣丁謂、王欽若啟上侈心之為也。

translations.literal: Because of illness he had not yet been received in audience and regretted that he could not state face to face what he had stored up; he therefore submitted a bold memorial saying: "In recent years the state treasury has been emptied and the living people's fat and blood exhausted to supply useless earth-and-wood projects—all the doing of treacherous ministers Ding Wei and Wang Qinruo in arousing the sovereign's extravagant heart."
translations.idiomatic: Too ill to appear at court, he lamented that he could not speak his mind in person and submitted a blunt memorial: "In recent years the treasury has been drained and the people bled dry to pay for useless temples and palaces—all because the traitorous ministers Ding Wei and Wang Qinruo fed the emperor's taste for extravagance."

sentences.zh: 不誅死，無以謝天下”」章三上，出知陳州。

translations.literal: "If they are not executed, there is no way to answer to all under Heaven." He submitted the memorial three times and was sent out to govern Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: "Unless they are put to death, there is no answering to the realm." He submitted the memorial three times and was sent out to govern Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，詠與青州傅霖少同學。

translations.literal: At first Yong and Fu Lin of Qing Prefecture had studied together in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had studied with Fu Lin of Qingzhou when they were young.

sentences.zh: 霖隱不仕。

translations.literal: Lin lived in seclusion and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin lived in seclusion and never entered official life.

sentences.zh: 詠既顯，求霖者三十年不可得，至是來謁。

translations.literal: After Yong had become prominent, he sought Lin for thirty years without obtaining him; at this time Lin came to pay a visit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yong had risen to fame he searched for Fu Lin for thirty years without success; now Fu Lin came to see him.

sentences.zh: 閽吏白傅霖請見，詠責之曰：「傅先生天下賢士，吾尚不得為友，汝何人，敢名之！

translations.literal: The gatekeeper announced that Fu Lin requested an audience; Yong rebuked him, saying: "Master Fu is a worthy man of all under Heaven; I am not yet fit to be his friend—who are you to call him by name!"
translations.idiomatic: When the gatekeeper announced that Fu Lin wished to see him, Yong scolded him: "Master Fu is a sage of the realm; I am not worthy to call him friend—who are you to speak his given name so casually!"

sentences.zh: 」霖笑曰：「別子一世尚爾邪，是豈知世間有傅霖者乎？

translations.literal: Lin laughed and said: "After parting from you for a lifetime you are still like this—do you really know that there is a Fu Lin in the world?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin laughed. "We have been apart a lifetime and you are still like this—do you even know there is such a person as Fu Lin in the world?"

sentences.zh: 」詠問：「昔何隱，今何出？

translations.literal: Yong asked: "Why did you hide away before, and why have you come out now?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong asked: "Why did you hide yourself before, and why have you come out now?"

sentences.zh: 」霖曰：「子將去矣，來報子爾。

translations.literal: Lin said: "You are about to depart; I came to tell you."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin said: "You are about to go; I came to tell you so."

sentences.zh: 」詠曰：「詠亦自知之。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Yong also knows it himself."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said: "I know that already."

sentences.zh: 」霖曰：「知復何言。

translations.literal: Lin said: "Knowing it, what more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Lin said: "If you know, what more is there to say?"

sentences.zh: 」翌日別去。

translations.literal: The next day they parted and he departed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they said farewell and Fu Lin left.

sentences.zh: 後一月而詠卒，年七十。

translations.literal: One month later Yong died, at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Yong died, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射，諡忠定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with posthumous title Loyal and Settled.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous name Zhongding, Loyal and Settled.

sentences.zh: 詠剛方自任，為治尚嚴猛，嘗有小吏忤詠，詠械其頸。

translations.literal: Yong was stern and self-reliant; in governing he favored severity and rigor. Once a petty clerk offended Yong, and Yong put a cangue on his neck.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was unyielding and self-willed, and his rule leaned toward severity. Once a junior clerk crossed him, and Yong clapped a cangue around his neck.

sentences.zh: 吏恚曰：「非斬某，此枷終不脫。

translations.literal: The clerk resentfully said: "Unless you execute me, this cangue will never come off."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk snarled: "Unless you cut off my head, this cangue will never come off."

sentences.zh: 」詠怒其悖，即斬之。

translations.literal: Yong, angered at his insolence, immediately beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged by the insolence, Yong had him beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 少學擊劍，慷慨好大言，樂為奇節。

translations.literal: In youth he studied swordplay, was bold and fond of grand speech, and delighted in extraordinary acts.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he trained in swordsmanship, spoke boldly and grandly, and loved striking deeds out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 有士人遊宦遠郡，為僕夫所持，且欲得其女為妻，士人者不能制。

translations.literal: There was a scholar serving in office in a distant prefecture who was controlled by his servant and who moreover wanted to take the scholar's daughter as wife; the scholar could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar serving in a distant prefecture fell under the thumb of his servant, who also demanded the man's daughter in marriage, and the scholar could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 詠遇於傳舍，知其事，即陽假此僕為馭，單騎出近郊，至林麓中，斬之而還。

translations.literal: Yong encountered them at a relay inn, learned of the affair, immediately pretended to borrow this servant as driver, rode alone out to the near suburbs, went into the wooded hills, beheaded him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yong met them at a relay inn, learned what had happened, borrowed the servant on the pretext of needing a driver, rode alone into the nearby hills, cut off his head, and came back.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂其友人曰：「張詠幸生明時，讀典墳以自律，不爾，則為何人邪？

translations.literal: He once said to a friend: "Zhang Yong is fortunate to be born in an enlightened age and reads the classics to restrain himself; otherwise, what sort of man would he be?"
translations.idiomatic: He once told a friend: "Zhang Yong is lucky to live in an enlightened age and holds himself in check by reading the classics—otherwise, what sort of man would he become?"

sentences.zh: 」故其言曰：「事君者廉不言貧，勤不言苦，忠不言己效，公不言己能，斯可以事君矣。

translations.literal: Hence his saying: "One who serves a ruler is upright yet does not speak of poverty, diligent yet does not speak of hardship, loyal yet does not speak of his own merit, impartial yet does not speak of his own ability—only thus may one serve a ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Hence his maxim: "In serving a ruler, be upright but do not speak of your poverty; be diligent but do not speak of your toil; be loyal but do not speak of your merit; be fair but do not speak of your talent—only then can you truly serve."

sentences.zh: 」性躁果卞急，病創甚，飲食則痛楚增劇，御下益峻，尤不喜人拜跪，命典客預戒止。

translations.literal: His nature was impetuous, fierce, and impatient; his wound was severe, and when he ate and drank the pain grew worse; he governed subordinates all the more sternly and especially disliked people bowing and kneeling, ordering the master of ceremonies to warn them in advance to stop.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature quick-tempered, fierce, and impatient; his wound grew worse whenever he ate, and he grew harsher with his staff. He particularly hated being bowed and knelt to, and ordered his protocol officer to warn visitors in advance.

sentences.zh: 有違者，詠即連拜不止，或倨坐罵之。

translations.literal: When anyone violated this, Yong would bow continuously without stopping, or sit aloof and revile him.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone disobeyed, Yong would bow back at them without pause, or sit haughtily and berate them.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗稱其材任將帥，以疾不盡其用。

translations.literal: Zhenzong once praised his talent as fit for command as a general, but because of illness his ability was not fully employed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong once said his talents were equal to a general's command, but illness kept him from full use.

sentences.zh: 自號「乖崖」，以為「乖」則違眾，「崖」不利物。

translations.literal: He styled himself Perverse Cliff, taking "perverse" to mean departing from the crowd and "cliff" to mean not benefiting things.
translations.idiomatic: He took the sobriquet "Perverse Cliff," explaining that to be perverse is to stand apart from the crowd, and a cliff is a place that benefits nothing.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to ten juan.

sentences.zh: 弟詵，為虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shen served as Vice Director in the Bureau of Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shen was Vice Director in the Bureau of Revenues.

sentences.zh: 論曰：《傳》云：「邦有道，危言危行。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Classic of History states: "When the state has the Way, speak dangerous words and walk a dangerous path."
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: The Classic says, "When the state is governed well, speak blunt truths and live by stern principles."

sentences.zh: 」三人者，躬骨鯁蹇諤之節，蔚為名臣，所遇之時然也。

translations.literal: These three men personally embodied the integrity of blunt remonstrance and forthright opposition, flourishing as famed ministers—it was the times they encountered that made it so.
translations.idiomatic: These three embodied unyielding integrity and fearless remonstrance and rose to fame as great ministers—such was the age they lived in.

sentences.zh: 禹偁製戎之策，厥後果符其言，而醇文奧學，為世宗仰。

translations.literal: Yucheng's policy for controlling the frontier afterward indeed matched his words, and with pure literary style and profound learning he was looked up to by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yucheng's frontier policy later proved exactly as he had foretold, and with his polished prose and deep learning the age looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 錫身沒之後，特降褒命，以賁直操，與夫容容嘿嘿，以持祿固位者異矣。

translations.literal: After Xi died, a special decree of praise was issued to adorn his upright conduct—unlike those who mumble agreeably and hold their salaries to secure their positions.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Xi's death a special decree honored his upright character—quite unlike those who murmur assent and cling to office for the salary.

sentences.zh: 詠所至以政績聞。

translations.literal: Wherever Yong went, he was renowned for his achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yong served, his administrative record made his name.

sentences.zh: 天子嘗曰：「詠在蜀，吾無西顧之憂。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven once said: "With Yong in Shu, I have no worry for the west."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said: "With Yong in Shu, I need not fear for the west."

sentences.zh: 」其被獎與如此。

translations.literal: Such was the praise and reward he received.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 然皆骯髒自信，道不諧偶，故不極於用云。

translations.literal: Yet all were stubbornly self-assured, their Way not harmonizing with others; therefore they were not employed to the fullest, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all were proud and uncompromising, ill suited to easy alliance with others, and so none was used to the full—such is the historians' verdict.
